name: qomplement
long_description:
qomplement is the agentic ERP for retail and logistics companies.

Retail and logistics are the industries with the highest volume of transactions in the world. POs, freight invoices, inventory updates, and shipment confirmations. Every single one still requires a person to process it manually. Their only solution has been hiring more people.

Legacy ERPs were built for humans. qomplement is the agentic ERP that cuts 95% of manual work and handles 100x more transactions with the same headcount. We give procurement and operations teams superpowers: automating purchase order intake, vendor onboarding, item master updates, freight order processing, carrier invoicing, three-way matching, and inventory reconciliation.

Headquartered in San Francisco.
one_liner: The Agentic ERP for supply chain operations

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
Kerim and Andres met in college studying computer science. They became friends trying to track a jaguar near their city. They placed cameras across the mountains, collected more than 15,000 minutes of footage, and quickly realized there was no way to review it all manually. That was their first real problem to solve with AI.

They spent the next few years building AI systems together at their university's research lab.

qomplement started with a phone call. One of the largest oil and gas companies in the world reached out with a problem that seemed almost too simple: they had more than 30 people whose entire job was moving data between systems all day.\
Kerim and Andres flew out immediately. They rented an apartment next to the client's office and spent a full month doing the work themselves. Every purchase order, every ERP update, every vendor portal, every email. They wanted to feel the problem before building anything.

That month became the foundation for qomplement.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
The global economy is roughly $100 trillion. Around $30 trillion of that is the physical economy, the movement of goods across retail, logistics, and supply chains. Yet this entire part of the economy still runs on legacy ERPs, spreadsheets, and large operations teams.

The problem is that these businesses scale by adding headcount. Every new PO, every invoice, every shipment confirmation requires a human to process manually. As headcount grows, human error compounds, processes slow down, and operations become a bottleneck to growth.

We discovered this firsthand. We flew out to one of the largest oil and gas companies in the world, rented an apartment next to their office, and spent a month doing the work ourselves. Every PO, every ERP update, every vendor email. 30 people whose entire job was moving data between systems all day. That month became the foundation for qomplement.

\
**What we're building**

qomplement is the agentic ERP for retail and logistics companies. We replace NetSuite and SAP with an AI-native system where agents handle the full workflow end to end, procurement, inventory, freight, and finance, without human input.\
We land with one high-pain module, prove value in weeks, and expand until we replace the entire ERP. Full migrations take 2 months instead of 12. Same team, 100x more transactions.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
SAP and NetSuite have dominated enterprise software for 30 years. Every company moving physical goods has built entire departments just to keep those systems running.

We're on a mission to end that. A world where no one hates their ERP. Where one person processes what used to take entire departments. Where the system does the work instead of just recording it.

qomplement is the agentic ERP replacing Oracle and NetSuite, built from the ground up for AI agents, not humans.

Hiring should match the right people to the right roles. It rarely does. Five failures repeat on every search, and almost no one escapes them.

* **Spam** — Talent fire hundreds of AI applications. Recruiters fire hundreds of AI messages. Both inboxes drown in noise.
* **Visibility** — Early stage founders struggle to reach the talent worth hiring. The best talent gets buried in the inbound. Both sides struggle to stand out.
* **Asymmetry** — Talent see titles and comp bands. Founders see resumes and LinkedIn. Neither side sees what actually matters.
* **Privacy** — Looking around means risking your current job. There's no way to say "I'm open" without saying "I'm leaving”
* **Cost** — Recruiters take 20–30% of first-year salary, after weeks of back-and-forth, and the role still goes to someone they didn't find.

Standout is an agentic hiring marketplace. Talent and companies each get an autonomous agent that represents them, vets the other side, and only makes the intro when the fit is real.

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
We started as Salesgraph, building agents and workflows for enterprise sales teams.

In enterprise sales, there are four bottlenecks: pipeline, execution, internal, and implementation

Pipeline: how can I do effective outreach to more people.

Execution: how can I boost deal win rate.

Internal: how can I make CPQ, deal-desk, approvals, and negotiations fast.

Implementation: how can I get new customers onboarded smoothly post-sale to avoid clawback.

We were working on execution first, because we solved that internally at Mintlify. After we started tackling pipeline generation, we realized that pipeline generation tools make great primitives for all research.

To build pipeline, you need to create tables of people and companies that you want to sell into. From those tables, you create primitives to dive deeper and do more specialized research to then build automations off of.

What if you want to do deeper research? Learn the industry that your pipeline is built on, map vertical bottlenecks to your solution, go deep on each person to see how they relate to you? Now, you’re going the extra mile to partner on a solution to a business problem with each client, not just features.

But what if you expand this past sales?

What if you’re in manufacturing and want to map supply chain bottlenecks to do better capacity planning?

What if you’re in finance and want to see what data-center construction is doing to grid prices in Texas and Louisiana?

What if you’re in R&D at a biotech and want to run virtual simulations overnight without hooking it up to your lab equipment.

This tool that we built for a niche use case of account research and pipeline generation turns out to be the perfect primitive for all research.

What if we built the best tools for agents to be able to run simulations, experiments, and research in collaboration autonomously.

We can then build the most intuitive way to give humans info from that research in a way they can digest and build a better flywheel.

We quickly went from asking how good can we make sales outreach more effective to asking how many people we can reach who have a question they can’t answer because they don’t have the tools or knowhow.

From building the tools to close revenue more effectively, we realized there's a much larger opportunity to build better tools for agents to answer any question.

As Antinuous, we are building an autonomous research platform where people can investigate their hardest questions and turn what they learn into action.

Hey we’re [Ruhan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ruhanponnada/) and [Ricardo](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ricardonunez-01/) - engineer turned seller, and seller turned engineer.

**Offer:** Get a free [GTM Audit ](https://www.salesgraph.com/gtm-audit)on your company or prospects + if you intro us to a closer, for a meeting booked, get free Lulu merch!\
\
**TL;DR** Salesgraph automates deal context and collateral for enterprise sales teams, so every rep walks into every call prepared and leaves every call with clear next steps. We're a headless UI, starting with a Slack-native experience that integrates with your CRM, calendar, call recordings, docs, blogs, case studies, and research.

<https://youtu.be/fO6c2wIPwIw>
\
**The Problem:**
Sales reps have too much on their plate: back-to-back meetings, Slack messages from prospects, follow-up emails, and coordination with SEs. The best reps balance this. The rest forget to follow up, come to calls unprepared, and lose deals at pricing because they can't value sell.\
\
This gets harder when you're selling a technical product as a non-technical rep. You can't articulate value if you don't fully understand what you're selling, so reps default to features, line items, and discounts.\
\
**The Result:** enterprise deals die in procurement. \
\
When reps walk in without a clear business case, procurement has all the leverage. Deals stall on price, ACV gets discounted away, or the deal dies entirely.

We lived this at Mintlify. Reps looked great on paper, but folded under pressure. The truth is, sales is as much nurturing as it is selling. The best reps act like consultants, not order takers.\
\
**Our Solution:** At an internal Mintlify hackathon, our Head of Sales paired with Ricardo to build an internal tool: a value case generator trained on call recordings, past deals, case studies, ROI calculators, and the MEDDIC framework. The output was a 3-page business case our champions used to sell Mintlify internally — driving higher ACVs and helping us close millions from enterprise logos.

Why can’t we evangelize every GTM team to close deals at higher ACV through encouraging value selling? \
\
We took those learnings to build Salesgraph.

In Slack, reps get proactive context 5 minutes before every call — triggers from background agents, key notes from previous calls, and what to cover next. After every call, they get a DM with strengths, gaps to address, and next steps.

We integrate with major call recorders and ship our own ambient recorder (a sales-focused alternative to Granola), **free for founders and teams under 3**.\
\
**Why this matters for everyone, not just reps:**

* **Sales managers** query deal state directly in Slack, no more reading low-quality opp notes or meaningless health scores
* **SEs and FDEs** stop watching call recordings at 2x speed; they just ask in Slack
* **Customer success** sees what was actually promised vs delivered

\
Every rep should sell like your best rep. \
\
Try us out <https://www.salesgraph.com/>.

Most people are focused on humans using AI to do digital work. We think the more exciting opportunity is AI creating and coordinating work in the physical economy.

Rentahuman lets AI agents communicate with and pay humans to do real-world tasks.

Our mission is to use AI to create new jobs and coordinate workers at global scale.

AI agents can code, write emails, use software, spend money, and complete increasingly complex digital tasks. But they still cannot record household chores for robotics training, capture in-store photos, find people for a video shoot, organize a local event, pick up supplies, or do the physical work required to operate in the real world. These are all use cases we have tackled at Rentahuman.

Most AI systems are trained and deployed inside the digital world. But the next generation of AI and robotics systems will need more than software tools. They will need structured data, local execution, and human participation from the physical world.

Rentahuman gives them a way to get it.

We are now using Rentahuman for live deployments, from data collection tasks for AI and robotics companies to operational experiments like an AI-managed laundromat. These deployments help us learn how agents hire workers, spend money, collect data, coordinate people, manage physical workflows, and recover from operational failures.

This is the beginning of a larger shift: AI agents moving from browsers and software tools into the real economy.

We believe AI will create demand for more human work, not less. The future will have more intelligence, more jobs, and more opportunities for people outside of the digital world.

Rentahuman is the marketplace where that future begins.

**TLDR:** Andco's AI agents run the entire pre-litigation workup for personal injury firms across every channel they use: fax, email, mail, web, SMS, and voice - so they can scale their firm without overhead.

**The first 24 hours of a case, with Andco**

The moment a PI firm signs a new client, a race starts. Police reports need to be pulled, insurers need to be called, medical providers need to be faxed (yes, still faxed). Our agents go off across all channels in parallel: requesting the police report, opening claims with carriers like Geico and Progressive, identifying UM/UIM coverage, engaging adjusters, requesting records and bills from every treating provider, and running follow-up cadences until everything lands. Roughly 8 hours of legal staff work, done before anyone at the firm sits down at their desk.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100597&key=user_uploads/1126674/72f429e1-75ec-45b9-8481-5fac0d0dce5a)

**The Problem**

Personal injury is a $50B+ industry, and firms live or die on pre-litigation workup speed. The problem: every case requires chasing dozens of documents from police departments, insurance carriers, and medical providers — most of whom still run on fax, mail, and phone. Firms have two options today

1. Hire armies of legal staff + paralegals (expensive, high turnover, caps your caseload)
2. Outsource to point-solution retrieval vendors (slow, opaque, expensive per-request)

Legal tech built for this has historically been document and case management systems — great for storing things, terrible at actually doing the work. Meanwhile AI tooling in PI has mostly focused on downstream workflows like medical chronologies and demand drafting, which still depend on someone else getting the case context in first.

**The Solution**

Andco runs the pre-lit workup end-to-end. We're the system that actually does the work of getting the context. Our agents operate across fax, email, mail, web, SMS, and voice - the same channels your legal staff uses, plus a few they can't scale on. We're live with PI firms across the US and are exploring pilots with the world's largest injury law firms.

Early results:

• 8 hours saved in the first 24 hours of a case

• 24+ hours saved between intake and demand

**About Us**

We're a team of repeat founders, ex-lawyers, and builders.

**Ryan Xue (CEO)** — previously founded Layup (W23, exited to Whatfix). Before that: Origin, McKinsey, Google.

**David Lee (CTO)** — 2x founder/CTO. Previously NoxuData and Seek.

launches.tagline: Production-mirror sandboxes with digital twins of every SaaS integration
launches.body:
**tl;dr:** **become a 100x tester** with Arga by giving your agents staging environments scoped to a change. We spin up twins of your integrations (Slack, Stripe, etc.) and dependencies (DB, Redis), and deploy only the services that were changed. Everything else is routed to prod.

Launch Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OzEk5pYTvak>

**The problem: You’re a 1x tester**

* You don’t have staging :(
* You have staging, but it’s different from prod, and things still break after testing
  * You mock integrations, which can be inaccurate
  * You use real accounts to test integrations, but you hit rate limits, can’t clear states between tests, and can’t test at scale
* You have staging, but your agents can’t automatically test changes so you’re stuck at being a 1x tester despite being a 100x engineer
* You have staging, but it’s difficult to merge concurrent changes without breaking something (for larger teams!)

**Our Solution**

We spin up a temporary staging of your app every time you open a PR. Only the services you change are redeployed; all other services are routed to prod. Your dependencies are deployed as in-memory sidecars, so nothing corrupts prod data. For example, you can configure the tests to read from the prod database and perform all write commands to the sidecar; you can also configure everything to be routed to the sidecar.

We also spin up twins of services your app uses: Stripe, Slack, GSuite, Hubspot, and more, so you don’t hit the real API. This lets you test more thoroughly: **you can catch weird edge cases, simulate failure modes, and run tests in parallel without worrying about rate limits.** All twins are fully compatible with any SDK, expose the same API endpoints, and support webhook events. You can seed any twin in natural language, or select from our pre-set scenarios.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99708&key=user_uploads/3010892/cf335c26-a032-4a1d-bcc1-6c4863946abc)

Demo of Github, Slack, Stripe twins on the Arga app: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3ZPrIdGvPoo>

You or your agent can prompt Arga via web, API, CLI, or MCP to **automatically generate tests for your PR, run them, and stream the results and logs back**. This allows them to know what was tested, what broke, and which calls/functions caused the failure. They can use this information to go back and fix the code, so you’ll have a fully-tested and passing PR before you look at it.

Validation report:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99708&key=user_uploads/3010892/81258740-df00-46e1-9ba9-b2bbfd7a4572)

Claude Code using arga CLI to read logs & test results:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=99708&key=user_uploads/3202471/286496d9-28f2-4c01-a186-35235ed55189)

**Our ask**

Try us out! We’re live at [www.argalabs.com](http://www.argalabs.com) and you can get access to limited features for free. \
If you like our stuff, book a demo here (<https://cal.com/phillip-li/30min>).\
If you know any teams that struggle with testing and use lots of external integrations, send them our way.

**The Team**

Akira and Phillip met each other in first-year calculus at UBC. At the time, Akira was 14 and Phillip was studying neuroscience to pursue research in human biology. Within a year of pivoting to CS, Phillip built a dev tool at Amazon that saved 10 weeks / year of engineering hours as an intern. While interning at Stripe, Akira realized that a high-fidelity “staging” was the key to unlocking dev productivity and was surprised that most companies don’t have proper staging that actually mirrored prod. Now they’re solving that problem.

launches.tagline: AI voice agents for enterprise contact centers running on legacy phone infrastructure
launches.body:
Hey YC,

We are Haithem and Chehir - co-founders of  [Callab AI](https://callab.ai/). 

**The problem**

The global call center industry is worth $400B, and about 58% of it still runs on on-prem PBX infrastructure like Cisco UCM, Mitel, and FreeSWITCH. These systems have been in place for 20 years, with millions invested in deploying and maintaining them. They work, and they're not going anywhere.

AI voice agents have been built on top of cloud telephony providers, which means every solution on the market today requires the customer to already be on cloud phone systems. If you're running on-prem, you're locked out. The only option is a full migration to cloud, which typically takes 12 to 18 months, costs a fortune, and frequently fails. Meanwhile, these same companies are dealing with 30 to 40% agent attrition rates, rising labor costs, and customers who won't tolerate hold times. They want automation but they simply can't access it.

That's a massive segment of a $400B market sitting there with no solution available to them.

**What we built**

Callab AI is a cloud-based AI voice platform that connects directly to on-prem PBX systems via SIP trunk integration. The phone system stays exactly where it is, calls get routed to our AI agents, handled, and returned. No rip-and-replace, no migration, and we go live in one week.

We automate up to 70% of inbound call volume across use cases like call routing, appointment scheduling, order status, and customer inquiries. The hard part is the integration layer itself, which requires going deep into legacy telecom infrastructure that most teams don't want to touch. We built it to work with any telephony stack, and that's what makes this possible.

We're YC P25 and currently expanding into the US, focused on hospitality, logistics, retail chains, and property management. Healthcare and financial services are on the roadmap once we complete HIPAA compliance.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101754&key=user_uploads/1938837/5d95733e-2ac9-45b4-8f2b-5ef8a8a3b8ca)

**How we got here**

We didn't set out to become the on-prem PBX company. We started building AI voice agents in the Middle East and Africa, where cloud telephony providers don't operate, SIP trunks are state-regulated, and every contact center runs legacy infrastructure. We had no choice but to build our integration layer to work directly with whatever phone system was already on the ground. After plugging into old telecom stacks, we realized the problem we solved out of necessity in MEA is the exact same problem sitting untouched in the US. The constraint that shaped our product in a harder market turned out to be a global advantage.

**How you can help**

If you know anyone at a company running a legacy phone system or on-prem contact center, we'd love an intro. Hotels, restaurant groups, logistics operators, large retail, or property management are all ideal. Also happy to connect with anyone who's worked with managed service providers, value-added resellers, or sold into enterprise telecom IT. Drop me a note.

Hey everyone 🙂

We’re [Tim](https://www.linkedin.com/in/timzinkl/) and [Matthias](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthias-wolf/), co-founders of Pairio

**TL:DR:**

**Machine downtime in manufacturing is expensive. Pairio helps technicians and operators resolve faults faster with voice AI.**

4 plants in Germany are already using Pairio to reduce equipment downtime.

**Ask:** Can you introduce us to plant and maintenance managers at US manufacturing firms? Contact us at [tim.zinkl@pairio.com](mailto:tim.zinkl@pairio.com)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kmUBOkAU33M>

**The Problem**

Unplanned equipment downtime costs global industries over $1.4 trillion every year – and the root cause isn't broken machines. It's broken knowledge transfer.

* When a machine fails, resolution speed depends almost entirely on whether the one guy who's seen this before is working that day
* Valuable technical clues are buried somewhere across 400 pages of OEM manuals or locked in outdated software
* After spending 6 hours getting the line back up, the last thing a technician does is sit down and write a detailed fault report to institutionalize their knowledge

With the average technician in the US now 50 years old, knowledge is literally walking out the door, further compounding the problem for years to come.

**Our Solution**

We have shown at 4 factories in Germany that removing these barriers can lead to higher equipment uptime – and the effect compounds with every fault processed with Pairio.

With our voice-first approach we empower technicians and operators to:

* Simply ask and instantly receive any available technical clue
* Speak and let Pairio structure their learnings into reusable know-how
* Use photos and videos to capture even more contextual knowledge

By focusing on capturing the reality on the shop floor we are building the foundation for agentic workflows that eliminate off the wrench time and optimize equipment uptime.

launches.body:
**TL;DR**: StableBrowse is the browser layer for AI agents. We transform dynamic websites into structured knowledge graphs that capture how sites truly work, giving agents persistent memory to complete tasks reliably without starting from scratch every time.

**Ask**: If you’re building agents that browse the web, scrape data, fill forms, monitor prices, or work inside authenticated portals, we’d love to talk! Reach us at [team@stablebrowse.ai](mailto:team@stablebrowse.ai) or schedule a demo at [stablebrowse.com](http://stablebrowse.com).

<https://youtu.be/ng_ZM1PCkv0?si=x4pVN9tEb5PNhfxv>

**Problem**: AI agents are increasingly being used for real web workflows like tracking competitor pricing, applying for loans, updating CRM records, booking travel, submitting expense reports, and navigating legacy enterprise systems.

Most browser agents still treat every interaction like it’s the first time, repeatedly asking an LLM what to click next. This works in demos, but breaks in production because websites constantly change through:

* Pop-ups and modal interruptions
* Login and authentication flows
* Slow-loading dropdowns and forms
* Layout and UI updates
* Dynamic page behavior

As a result, agents become unreliable, expensive to run, and difficult to scale across real-world workflows.

**Solution**: StableBrowse gives AI agents persistent memory of how websites actually work by converting websites into structured execution graphs. Instead of rediscovering workflows every run, StableBrowse learns websites once and reuses that knowledge across future executions.

We convert pages into structured states, turn buttons and forms into reliable actions, extract clean structured data instead of raw HTML, and detect when websites change to keep workflows reliable over time.

At runtime, StableBrowse handles:

* Navigating known workflows
* Filling forms and completing submissions
* Extracting clean, structured data
* Handling date pickers and dropdowns
* Detecting when websites change
* Returning usable outputs instead of raw HTML

This allows the LLM to focus on user intent instead of fragile browser interactions. The results are dramatic: 70–80% lower token usage, 3–4× faster workflows, and up to 98% success rate.

\

long_description:
In investment management, every decision gets graded. The market prints the answer on a date known in advance, and nobody gets to argue with it.

Kimpton is financial AI that answers to reality. Kimpton OS is the AI-native operating system for investment teams: it does the research and hands PMs structured trades. EarningsBench is a public benchmark where models forecast quarterly earnings before companies report and the reported numbers do the scoring. Koliseum is the set of point-in-time financial environments we build from that work, for labs to train and evaluate models on.

The whole industry is fighting underperformance. Active managers trail their benchmarks, and capital keeps bleeding into passive. AI was supposed to fix that, but it hasn't. Funds either stitch together a dozen point tools or babysit general agents all day, and neither gets them to the trade.

Kimpton OS goes straight to it. It ingests a fund's mandate, strategy, and positions, connects to the institutional data the fund already runs on, and returns a structured trade proposal built for that fund. It's built to disagree, because consensus is poison for investment decisions. Instead of telling a PM what they want to hear, it surfaces the breaches and risks they'd otherwise miss.

That same work is how we grade AI. Static benchmarks leak into training data. Simulations reward what their authors imagined. A forecast sealed before the outcome exists and scored when the company reports can't be rehearsed or backdated. We started in markets because they're the one place reality answers on schedule.

We're two ex-Goldman engineers and an ex-SpaceX engineer. We left to start our own quantitative systematic hedge fund, raised $10M from a family office at 21 and 22, and scaled it to $35M over four years. We learned to trust live results over historical fit. We built Kimpton inside that fund, then productized the stack.

We're live with our first institutional client, a $3.3B manager. Our first market is fundamental equity funds from $1B to $10B, and the labs that need to know whether their models can do this work.

launches.title: Koliseum by Kimpton, Live Evaluation Arenas for AI Models
launches.tagline: Real-world market interaction environments, starting with financial markets
launches.body:
Today we're launching **Koliseum** by [Kimpton](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/31420), live evaluation arenas for AI models in financial work.

**The problem**

Static benchmarks are contaminated soon after publication, and simulations reward the assumptions their designers encode. 

This simply isn't acceptable in finance or any other professional industry. A wrong answer or action can be catastrophic and reality eventually shows whether the claim was right. Almost no evaluation waits to find out.

**Koliseum**

Before Kimpton, we ran a quantitative fund. Backtests never proved alpha; live markets did. Koliseum applies the same test to models: a model commits inside an arena, the record is sealed, and reality supplies the grade.

Two kinds of arenas:

* **Prediction Arenas** seal a forecast before the outcome exists and score it against consensus, market, and statistical baselines when reality resolves.
* **Action Arenas** give a model a bounded task and real tools, then verify success from the resulting system state.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=113565&key=user_uploads/3054189/789d031b-cca8-4596-8921-dbc9f1544cb4)

The first Prediction Arena is already running. **EarningsBench** seals earnings forecasts for public companies 24 hours before each release and scores them against consensus and a statistical baseline once results are public.

Two things are already clear: most open-weight models reproduce consensus exactly, and a simple statistical baseline is harder to beat than a leaderboard alone would suggest.

Along with these developments, we are introducing a new concept in evaluation: **reality-as-a-judge**.

![uploaded image](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=113565&key=user_uploads%2F3054189%2Fc6c1ba2c-4e77-4ebc-be71-675f0abd71a6&variant=large)

Most open-ended evaluations are graded by another model or by a human rubric, so the score inherits the grader's assumptions. In reality-as-a-judge, the grader is the outcome itself.

[More info on Koliseum](https://www.kimpton.ai/koliseum)

[Methodology](https://www.kimpton.ai/methodology)

**Our ask**

Reach out if:

* You work on post-training or evals at a lab and want your model in the first private cohort. Results stay private unless you publish them.
* You run a trading firm or a prediction venue and want models scored on your own resolving questions, or want to co-run a public arena.
* You have a workflow (any industry!) with a verifiable end state and want it turned into an Action Arena.

or know anyone who does.

Write to us at [founders@kimpton.ai](mailto:founders@kimpton.ai). Thanks for the support!

launches.title: Kimpton: Cursor for portfolio managers
launches.tagline: AI-native terminal where agents do the research and propose the trades
launches.body:
**TL;DR** AI can’t trade, but portfolio managers can. Kimpton combines high-resolution public financial markets data, portfolio manager strategy/mandate, portfolio holdings, and transaction data to generate trade ideas for managers.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3aED4nL3G50>

**Our Background**

We are former Goldman Sachs and Vistra Energy engineers who started a quantitative hedge fund together in 2021 after raising $10M from a family office at the ages of 22 and 21 years old, scaling it to $35M at its peak.

We spent four years systematically trading using the tools that we built in-house to support our systems. Internally, we developed Kimpton to automate many of our own workflows.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102078&key=user_uploads/3054189/7f252d74-65d7-4557-92f0-59383e3a782a)

**The Problem**

AI can’t trade. After all, LLMs are the most overfit backtest in all of human history. They are consensus machines and sycophantic by nature. As a result, AI goes largely unused by portfolio managers today.

Agents finally had depth in 2025. We tested LLMs on the markets and were unimpressed with the output. LLMs can’t trade because they are consensus machines and sycophantic by nature. They lack the edge that portfolio managers provide.

AI can’t trade like a portfolio manager, but they can research at 100X the efficiency of an investment analyst. For this reason, Kimpton revolves around the portfolio manager, solving increasingly all of the workflows that they need.

Analysts spend weeks aggregating data and synthesizing it to generate singular trade ideas that are passed up to portfolio managers for review. It’s time for a change.

Investment management is built on the idea that analysts and PMs need to spend their days staring at screens all day to find edge in the markets. 

To refactor the investment management industry, we can’t simply provide better tools. We have to automate the entire research layer instead.

**The Solution**

Kimpton automates the analysis layer by securely ingesting firm-wide context, portfolio, and transaction data to synthesize fully-formed trade recommendations fitted to their portfolio.

Portfolio managers can challenge the results of the trade proposals through a process we call Adversarial Review, an agentic Socratic questioning to assist portfolio managers in coming to their own conclusions.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102078&key=user_uploads/3054189/62ecf56b-91f8-4c4d-a883-6a8be7df6108)

We developed a harness specifically for the financial markets to make aggregation efficient, fast, and accurate. It has access to high-quality institutional data sources through Factset, Massive, and Tiingo. Real-time data on tens of thousands of global assets across equities, ETFs, indices, insider trades, SEC filings, events, transcripts, company fundamentals, corporate leadership, and more!

Our AI agents also provide portfolio managers with the ability to generate many different types of artifacts, such as real-time dashboards, institutional-grade reports, and comprehensive visualizations.

**Traction**

Kimpton is deployed and generating trade proposals on billions of dollars of assets under management today.

Portfolio managers are using Kimpton to monitor their exposures, understand investment thesis drift, earnings coverage, manage positioning across teams, investor reporting, and as an investment team collective brain.

Portfolio managers are underserved today when the potential to refactor the way they work is massive. Kimpton is focused on improving the lives portfolio managers who are actively making decisions in the public markets.

**Ask**

If you know anyone who manages assets a hedge fund, family office, mutual fund, ETF manager, or other public markets manager — we’d love to speak with them.

launches.tagline: The Fastest Way to Generate Whiteboard Explainer Videos from a Single Prompt or Documents
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Simi is the fastest, easiest, and most cost-effective way to create whiteboard explainer videos. You give it a prompt or a document. It writes the script, draws the illustrations, animates them, adds narration, and hands you a finished video in seconds. Anything from a one minute short to a full hour, in one shot, in 80+ languages. Built by Lamina Labs (YC P26). Use it through the app or the API for training, onboarding, product walkthroughs, sales, marketing, and education at <https://laminalabs.ai>.

Here is an explainer video about Lamina Labs: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RLuOCdamcHE>

## Why we built this

AI video right now is built to look like a movie, not to explain something.

But most of the video people actually need at work is the boring kind. A training module. An onboarding flow. A walkthrough of the feature you shipped last week. And making one of those is absurdly slow. You either pay an agency thousands of dollars and wait weeks, or you sit in a template editor dragging boxes around for an afternoon and it still looks like you dragged boxes around.

That is fine if you need one video. It falls apart the moment you need a hundred. A course. Every feature documented. Onboarding in every language your customers speak. Anyone who has priced that out knows the math does not work.

## How it works

You type what you want. Simi writes the script, draws and animates it, and gives you a properly narrated video in seconds.

That is the whole thing. No storyboard, no timeline, no boxes to drag. Type "explain how photosynthesis works," or hand it a long compliance doc, and you get a finished video, not a draft. And it does not choke on length. One minute to a full hour, generated in a single shot.

If your team makes videos, you should be using this.

## What people make with it

Training and onboarding videos from the docs you already have. Product walkthroughs, one per feature, updated as fast as the product changes. Sales and marketing explainers, in every market you sell into. Course and lecture videos in the Khan Academy style. Faceless YouTube channels and localized social video at volume. Agencies run it through the API to produce explainer videos for their clients.

## What makes it different

An agency gives you a video in weeks for thousands of dollars. Simi gives you the same video in seconds for a fraction of that. That is the whole pitch, and it is enough.

A few things worth knowing beyond speed. It generates anything from a minute to an hour in one shot. It speaks 80+ languages, so you write once and localize everywhere. And it is built to plug in. Use the app, call the API from your own product, or run it inside agent frameworks like OpenClaw and Nous Research's Hermes.

## Who we are

We are Sudip and Kartikesh, the founders of Lamina Labs, and Simi is the first thing we have built. We are both from Nepal. We met at MIT and started building together there. We are the first Nepalese founding team to go through YC.

Simi is named after Simikot, the Himalayan village where Sudip grew up. We started with education because that is where this problem hurt us personally. But it is everywhere. Any time someone needs to turn an idea into a clear picture, that is us.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=104668&key=user_uploads/2592448/ddd4246e-1dae-4302-8e33-7c51d0264d6b)

## Our asks

If your team spends real money or real time making explainer, training, or onboarding videos, talk to us: [founder@laminalabs.ai](mailto:founder@laminalabs.ai)

We would love intros to L&D leaders, to agencies making video at volume, and to founders who want video generation inside their own product through the API.

And if you just want a video explaining your own startup, **try it:** <https://app.laminalabs.ai> \
**Learn more:** <https://laminalabs.ai>

launches.body:
# **BentoLabs AI: the monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents**

**TL;DR**: BentoLabs AI is the monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents. We detect when agents silently fail or drift from the user's goal, system prompt, or tool contracts, show affected users and root cause, and suggest the prompt, skill, or harness fix. Run 101 is measurably better than run 1.

<https://youtu.be/nu6Oir3OGSM>\
\
Hello everyone, we're Abhinav and Kaushik, co-founders of BentoLabs AI.

After spending two years at Emergent (YC S24), building and operating production coding agents used by 5M+ users, helping scale from 0 to $100M ARR and topping SWE-Bench twice. We realised as more teams deploy agents, keeping them reliable, observable, debuggable and continuously improving in production becomes mission-critical. Most teams don't have a system for it. They have engineers.

### **The Problem:**

Most production agents fail silently. You have 10,000 traces a day and zero visibility into reasoning drift until a support ticket pops up. That's the easier half! The harder problem is that nothing your agent figures out on one run carries into the next. An agent might solve a complex edge case on run 47, but because nothing carries forward, it burns your budget rediscovering the same fix on run 48.

This makes production teams spend hours reading logs in one tab just to manually patch prompts in another, on a loop that never closes.

### **The Solution:**

**BentoLabs AI** The monitoring and learning layer for long-running agents.

**Monitoring:** BentoLabs finds every failure instance across your production traces, classifies it, and tracks it before the support ticket pops up.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/55f2be9c-2363-4f4d-b3cc-98e803c9dbe6)

**Learning:** BentoLabs captures what your agent figures out on every run and makes sure it carries into the next one. Recurring failures get fixed once and stay fixed. Hard-won solutions become reusable. Run 101 starts from everything runs 1 through 100 learned, not from zero.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/84d43836-11f5-4684-9465-8b02ab715a52)

### **The Proof:**

**Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Internal Run):** we validated our recursive learning engine on Terminal-Bench 2.0, one of the most demanding agentic-shell benchmarks in the field today. Where the official Claude Sonnet 4.5 baseline scores 42.2% pass@1. Our agent scored 52.4%, with the same agent, same model, same budget.A +10.2 percentage-point lift, statistically significant (p < 0.05), with 13 tasks showing wins ≥ +20 pp and only 3 showing losses ([Deep Dive](https://bentolabs.ai/blog/tb2-recursive-learning-lift))

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/016f2897-dcb5-4137-a658-98e0e7ccf525)

\
**ARC-AGI-3 (Internal Run):** To see our engine in action, we took on ARC-AGI-3 (25 interactive puzzle games, the hardest agent benchmark we could find). While frontier models score 0.2–0.3% out of the box, 3 games the agent had never solved across \~30 prior runs were cracked for the first time. ([Deep Dive](https://bentolabs.ai/blog/self-learning-ai-agents-arc-agi))

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102358&key=user_uploads/2390820/3c51a5a5-c620-41f6-9ae0-23d9f3dda903)

**Why we're building BentoLabs**

We were the engineers who were the fix for the last 2 years at Emergent, where we spent thousands of hours staring at traces, and watching teams burn hours of their best engineers' time on patching prompts, correcting tool definitions and experimenting with different skills, hoping something will stick. We are building [BentoLabs AI](https://bentolabs.ai/) to move past this repetitive cycle.

We're already working with teams at unicorn scale. Every conversation with a team running agents in production confirms the same thing: the problem is universal. BentoLabs gives them the operational leverage to scale their agent ecosystems without scaling human firefighting alongside them.

If your engineers are doing the logs-and-patches rotation or your agents keep hitting the same failures, let's have a [chat.](https://cal.com/team/bentolabs-ai/platform-demo?overlayCalendar=true) Or Email: [abhinav@bentolabs.ai](mailto:abhinav@bentolabs.ai)/ [kaushik@bentolabs.ai](mailto:kaushik@bentolabs.ai)

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
Max led process optimization at Porsche. David built data pipelines in finance. Leon built AI automations at consultancies. They all noticed critical knowledge is trapped inside people's heads and never reaches the people who need it.

The team then felt inspired to work on the problem after a tour to Stockholms fastest scaling startups organized by Max, where all three decided to quit their jobs and start a company.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Every company already has the answers to most of the questions leadership is asking.

The problem: those answers are scattered across hundreds of people, and there's never been a practical way to ask every single employee.

So leaders make crucial decisions with partial information or spend months and millions on external consultants to retrieve what the org already knows.

**What we're building**

Ontora is an AI agent that has a real conversation with every employee in your company within hours.

It learns, follows up, and surfaces what people actually do and where they get stuck.

We deliver two things: a synthesized answer to the specific question leadership couldn't crack in their last business review (themed insights, process maps, automation roadmap with ROI), and a continuously refreshed operational context that humans and AI agents can both reason over.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Answers in hours instead of months. We imagine truly intelligence native companies that unlock the last proprietary data source left in the enterprise: operational knowledge living in your employees heads.

Enabling cost reduction, post-merger integration, and AI transformation… within hours and at a fraction of the cost of traditional consulting.

Every company we talk to has the same story: they bought Claude licenses for their teams but merely use it to rewrite emails. The AI transformation stalled because nobody mapped what to actually automate.

That's the real bottleneck. Not code. Context.

A 800-person European media agency flew to San Francisco to meet us after realizing they'd need 4-5 months and a team of consultants just to understand their own operations. With Ontora, they can map their entire company in days.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102685&key=user_uploads/1178744/2bd9ca28-443a-46ef-af8c-ad76dd2d6a9f)

Ontora deploys AI agents that interview every employee in your company -- not once, but continuously -- to map out how work actually gets done. We turn that into a living context layer that your AI agents can act on.

What used to take a consulting firm 4 months and 50-100 manual interviews, Ontora does in days. And because interviews run continuously, your context layer never goes stale. Your organization keeps learning about itself.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102685&key=user_uploads/1178744/56b07749-ae1e-4244-9064-d1dd122baecc)

Here's how it works:

1. **Deploy** -- Ontora's AI agents reach out to employees across your org through async interviews, meeting them where they work
2. **Map** -- Every interview extracts processes, decision rules, tools used, handoffs, and tribal knowledge into structured operational maps
3. **Act** -- The living context layer feeds directly into your AI agents and automations so they have the real-world context they need to perform

<https://youtu.be/Culdmbt9uPE>

* If your mid-market company (200-2,000 employees) is planning AI transformation...
* If your PE/VC firm wants to drive efficiency across portfolio companies...
* If your company spent 6 figures on consultants to map processes...

...we need to talk.

Hey everyone 👋

We're **Avi** and **Ritesh** — co-founders of **Oddpool**.

**TL;DR**

Oddpool helps quant and institutional desks harness the power of prediction markets. We make it easy to access, search, and analyze every venue from one place with the depth and history serious desks need.

**Ask:**  If you're a quant fund, prop shop, market maker, or hedge fund using prediction markets data (or thinking about it), we'd love to talk. Reach us at [founders@oddpool.com](mailto:founders@oddpool.com)

<https://youtu.be/dSG7gVU1M7w>

**The Problem**

Data is the lifeblood of modern finance. Every desk, every strategy, every edge starts with it.

Yet prediction markets, one of the fastest-growing asset classes in the world, still lack the tooling that makes every other asset class easy for desks to adopt, leaving anyone trying to use this data stuck with three major pains:

1. Fragmentation across venues with no shared symbology
2. No tick-level history to backtest against
3. Weeks spent normalizing data instead of generating signals

These compound the moment real money tries to enter, leaving a glaring problem to be solved.

**Our Solution**

Oddpool provides a frictionless experience to start pulling, backtesting, and building on prediction market data from day one.

launches.tagline: The AI coworker that helps pathologists work cases faster
launches.body:
Hey YC,

We’re Michael, Josiah, and Henry, co-founders of Voquill.

**TLDR:** Voquill is an AI coworker that helps pathologists write cases faster using their voice. Over the last 4 weeks. We’ve onboarded 25+ pathologists.

<https://youtu.be/Iw3n94o52Js>

**The Problem:** 

Pathologists are doctors who diagnose diseases by looking at tissues, cells, and fluids. They spend their whole day looking through a microscope, observing patterns, and then documenting their findings. These reports can be repetitive and tedious. **Pathologists bill a total of $30-$40BN each year** **yet a third of that spend goes to documentation**, not diagnosis, which is a massive drag on a field that's already short-staffed.

**Our Solution:**

Voquill is an AI coworker that helps pathologists write their reports faster. Think of it like an AI resident that listens to the pathologist as they work the case and drafts the report automatically. It learns the pathologists reporting style from their old cases, and ensures every report meets the bar for quality. We go beyond dictation and don't generate a transcript, but a finished sign-out ready report instead. This enables pathologists to spend more time on patient outcomes and sign out more cases.

There is already a shortage of pathologists when compared to the case demand. **This gap is expected to increase to 25% over the next decade.** We’re building Voquill to give pathologists the tools they need to work faster. 

**One More Thing:**

Voquill is being used by 25 pathologists from a leading F500 lab, saving each one \~20% in case writing time every day. We started with voice reporting because it's the highest-leverage moment in the workflow. We’ve since found that it's also the right moment to fix billing: as pathologists describe what they see, **Voquill suggests the optimal CPT codes, helping labs capture more of the $8B+ they currently leave on the table.**  

**The Team:**

Michael and Josiah previously worked at Techcyte, where they led the AI team and architected digital pathology systems. Henry was a Principal at Oliver Wyman, building AI and automation tools for F500 firms.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101652&key=user_uploads/3291143/12ea3b4b-4f60-4a6a-8e43-07d68b0eb511)

If you know any pathology labs or pathologists that sign out cases, please introduce us by emailing michael@voquill.com. Or, book a demo [here](https://calendly.com/michael-voquill/voquill-demo).

launches.body:
**TLDR**: Adialante builds compact and mobile whole-body MRIs. We already have $12.75M in LOIs, $30k in deposits, and our first system will be scanning by demo day.

---

##### **About Us:**

<https://youtu.be/iiRwpHPFIeM>\
\
"Disruptive Innovation describes a process by which a product or service takes root in simple applications at the bottom of the market — typically by being less expensive and more accessible — and then relentlessly moves upmarket, eventually displacing established competitors." — Christensen Institute

We’re [@Efrain Torres](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1230366) and [@Parker Jenkins](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1298954), the co-founders of [@Adialante](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/31434). We met on the first floor of our engineering dorm. And when we learned what disruptive innovation was, it captured us immediately. But what to disrupt? Trained as biomedical engineers, we both learned about MRI and were in awe of the clinical value. It can diagnose cancers, strokes, dementia, and more. Yet everyone said the same thing: MRI is not accessible.

So we knew what we had to do: disrupt the industry.

Over the past six years, we've invented new ways to do MRI, won millions in competitive grants, published research, secured patents (#12,625,209, #12,372,595, more to come), and built a team. And, now, we’re well on our way to disrupting the industry.

##### **Problem:**

We know how to 10x cancer outcomes: **you catch it early**. MRI is the most powerful cancer-detection tool in the world, yet systems cost millions to purchase, take months to install, and require high levels of technical skill. The result? We only use MRI when it's too late.

##### **Our solution:**

We've redesigned MRI from the ground up with new physics, algorithms, and hardware, all to bring cancer screening to all of us. Our MRIs:

* use 50% less hardware
* are 40% shorter and 80% lighter
* are whisper-quiet and much less claustrophobic
* and require no specialized infrastructure

All while maintaining the diagnostic quality patients need.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/e7c9bf11-8868-457b-aced-78bd369559f5)

But like Waymo, we won't sell our hardware — we'll own and operate it. We'll bring our MRIs to clinics in mobile trailers, handle its operations, and continuously improve our AI software after every scan. We're an imaging clinic on wheels. So instead of a clinic waiting months and paying millions, clinics will wait hours and pay hundreds.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/31ce218b-56df-4fc3-9450-5af5eea83895)

---

We're starting with prostate cancer. **Over 1M men every year require an MRI before a prostate biopsy, but virtually none of the urology clinics that treat them can offer one.**

After our per-scan fee, a clinic will collect the insurance reimbursement and make a profit. It's a win-win-win: we get the recurring revenue, they get a new revenue stream, and patients get the best imaging technology in the world. From there, the same piece of hardware expands to renal, breast, and brain scanning **until annual screening for high-risk cancers is the norm, not the exception.**

**Traction:**

* 6 clinics signed up
* $12.75M in LOIs for scanner utilization
* $30k deposited from a top ten urology clinic to reserve their spot in line
* MRI assembled

  ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101289&key=user_uploads/1230366/1fa5afed-cb5b-4f8d-a3f0-46a430043c0e)

launches.title: Lumius — The 3D Camera for the Body
launches.tagline: Fast, smart, accessible 3D ultrasound for everyone
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Lumius is making real-time, accessible, and intelligent 3D ultrasound to advance beyond today’s widely used 2D ultrasound (500 million scans annually). Our vision is to make 3D ultrasound a universal camera for the body.

<https://youtu.be/bWlJD4_Bx4k>

**Backstory**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101060&key=user_uploads/3059826/d6bfe836-eb86-43cf-af8f-cf653183cebc)

Luca Menozzi, Chenhang Li, and I bonded over ultrasound during our PhDs at Duke. For years, it has bothered us that ultrasound looks largely the same as it did decades ago. It is safer and more accessible than imaging tools like PET, CT, or MRI, yet it has never quite become as widely used in everyday care as it should be.

**The Problem**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101060&key=user_uploads/3059826/a37bfe1d-0a2f-4738-ac51-c7628335098e)

The vast majority of ultrasound imaging today is still 2D. Clinicians have to maneuver a probe while mentally reconstructing 3D anatomy from flat images. That makes ultrasound hard to learn and difficult to use, especially for newer clinicians.  3D ultrasound does exist today, mainly for cardiac and fetal imaging, but current systems cost roughly 10x more than standard 2D ultrasound machines.

**The Solution**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101060&key=user_uploads/3059826/63de8f91-ad1d-4cd2-abdc-cbd2461fcd5f)

Our tech shows a clear on-the-fly 3D view of what's inside the body with AI assistance. Instead of relying on thin 2D slices, users see the full volume in context, eliminating the 2D guesswork that makes ultrasound difficult to use. 

Our device will be affordable, compact, and portable. AI integration will also make it context-aware and intelligent, guiding users by explaining what they’re seeing and what to do next. For example, automatically detecting and extracting blood vessels, nerves, muscle, and more. 

We're starting with vascular access, particularly central line placement. This is a procedure where \~50% of first attempts fail, especially among new clinicians. And hospitals spend millions each year training clinicians on 2D ultrasound. From there, we will expand to blood clot detection, nerve block imaging, tumor diagnosis, and biopsy guidance. Our long-term vision is to make 3D ultrasound a universal camera for the body, accessible to everyone. 

**Our Asks**

We'd love to hear from:

* **Clinicians and hospital innovation teams** dealing with vascular access, nerve blocks, and/or ultrasound-guided procedures
* **Med device innovators** or anyone in the healthcare/medtech space that are interested in 3D imaging guidance
* **Anyone with feedback** on medical imaging, hardware, or FDA pathways

Please reach out to us at [contact@lumius-imaging.com](mailto:contact@lumius-imaging.com) or [book a quick call](https://calendly.com/contact-lumius-imaging/30min)

Sources: <https://bjcardio.co.uk/2008/01/ultrasound-guided-central-venous-access/> <https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Rapid-Femoral-Vein-Assessment-(RaFeVA)%3A-A-protocol-Brescia-Pittiruti/fade5949934e6e5a0fdaa8e798d5bf89934f9c50/figure/8> <https://academic.oup.com/academicmedicine/article-abstract/85/9/1462/8353240>

launches.body:
# 

**TL;DR**\
[Prototyping.io](http://Prototyping.io) is rebuilding the design-to-manufacturing workflow from the ground up with an AI-driven approach, automating the path from CAD design to production at scale.

<https://youtu.be/q8G9q_MEzug>

**The Problem**\
Over $1T is spent annually on mechanical part manufacturing, yet the process remains largely manual.

Getting parts made still takes weeks, often with high costs and inconsistent quality. Manufacturers spend days on DFM, sourcing, programming, and setup planning before production even starts. These delays slow hardware companies down and stretch product iteration cycles.

Building locally is still expensive, largely due to fragmented operations and low machine utilization. Many companies look offshore for lower pricing, but shipping timelines, tariffs, and supply chain delays often slow product development even further.

**What We’re Building**

[Prototyping.io](http://Prototyping.io) is building autonomous manufacturing for mechanical parts by automating the workflow between CAD designs and finished parts.

The workflow today looks like:

CAD → DFM → Planning → Sourcing → Programming → Setups → Manufacturing Execution

This workflow is being rebuilt with AI-native systems and physical AI models for manufacturing.

Our approach combines AI-driven manufacturing intelligence, workflow automation, and eventually autonomous execution through industrial robotics and highly automated production systems. The goal is to dramatically reduce lead times, improve quality consistency, and enable more efficient manufacturing at scale.

**What We’re Seeing**

Demand for faster and more reliable manufacturing is growing across robotics, AI infrastructure, energy, automotive, defense, and other industries.

We’re already helping companies ranging from early-stage startups to multi-billion dollar enterprises reduce hardware iteration cycles from weeks to days by delivering high-quality parts for prototyping and early production.

**If This Resonates**

If you’re building hardware and want to move faster, we’d love to work with you.

If you’re interested in robotics, physical AI, manufacturing automation, or autonomous manufacturing and want to join the [Prototyping.io](http://Prototyping.io) team, we’d love to talk.

launches.body:
**_TLDR:_** Result is a platform for entrepreneurs to start and operate businesses end-to-end. We take users from an idea to building the product, accepting payments, incorporation, and marketing. Our 8 private beta users collectively do $2.8M ARR.

Hi YC, [Aaryan Kushwah](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aaryan-kushwah) and [Savio Martin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/saviomartin/) made their first money on the internet starting businesses + side projects, and today **more people _than ever_** are starting businesses.

We will be where solopreneurs, indiehackers, creative founders, and content creators make _their first internet dollar. **Result is the operating system to start the next generation of businesses.**_

**Let's make our first internet dollar in this post**.

1\. **Build** - you start using Result _with or without_ a product, let's assume we don’t have one right now

In this example, we’re building [1600.lol](http://1600.lol) → an SAT learning tool with real past paper questions.

Result can build apps **with payment gateways**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102824&key=user_uploads/1610709/fd663606-9301-47ba-8ae8-143ab3786036)

We have our **_own_** payment gateway provider with **custom endpoints** to give each user their own payment gateway, keep record of payments, and we’re also working with them to provide **_tax filing capabilities_**.

If you already have a product built you can connect your existing Github repo and Result will have context, or if you’re a business that doesn’t need a product (service, consulting, etc.) you don’t need to connect anything!

2\. Simultaneously, it’s going to lock in a **brand** for the business.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102824&key=user_uploads/1610709/8dc92a8c-cd3a-4d8b-9b96-4cbd1d4005fc)

3\. **Sell -** Let’s start selling. First, Result helps you rank better on SEO and then creates content for you to post: reels, blogs, posts and whatever works specifically for your niche.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102824&key=user_uploads/1610709/0599fbb0-525e-4cb4-9932-023f728806ad)

This is a fan favorite feature, **_Tinder for marketing posts_**:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102824&key=user_uploads/1610709/bfd69287-1887-4b9e-9f99-4cdd51faf28a)

4\. **Incorporate** - At this point, once we’re confident the product is doing well → let’s make this a real business. **_You can incorporate on the platform_**. We have a relationship with a registered agent for a whitelabelled service. We’re working extremely hard on this and will be able to incorporate companies **_directly from chat, through an agent, or even through Claude Code._**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102824&key=user_uploads/1610709/ca4b1fa5-4a5f-4cec-8ebb-03b139bbdf6f)

5\. **Analyze** - our biggest advantage of owning the entire flow is **_attribution, cross-data analytics_** and actually driving **_meaningful revenue-boosting insights_**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102824&key=user_uploads/1610709/02885b15-1a2f-4490-a6cf-f3d3c06cd262)

We’re working on some really cool architecture for attribution, our goal is to be able to generate insights like:

1. This specific format of a social media post drew 10x more views but it targeted the wrong ICP so it converted only 10%, whereas this post that didn’t draw as many views converted better because it was a better target.
2. The comments on this post resonate with customer support emails requesting this feature and it should be built instead of what the codebase has in place of it.\
   \
   **_Context_** - Where does all this information go? Company Brain!

Starting a company on a single platform from scratch gives us a unique place to retain context of the entire business from Day 1. A lot of companies are trying to build company brains for existing businesses, we decided that starting on Day 1 for a new business is the new meta.

As you operate the business on the platform, the platform learns about your business and continues to become better.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102824&key=user_uploads/1610709/d2adb3d2-53aa-4215-8779-25bfcd5db9f1)

This is how [1600.lol](http://1600.lol) is operated on Result. [1600.lol](http://1600.lol) now does $1200 MRR and is operated from Result. **_You can see how it performs at [lab.result.dev](http://lab.result.dev)_**.

We’re in private beta and **our first 8 users collectively do $2.8M ARR.**

**_Asks:_**

* If you've built side projects, small businesses before, we'd love to get in touch and show you around!
* If you know thought leaders or friends in the space (solopreneurship, indiehacking, etc.) we'd love to talk to them to learn more about what they need.
* If you have experience live-streaming, know teams behind subathons, long-duration live streaming etc, we'd love to learn more for a challenge we're starting in July!

launches.body:
**TLDR: Mount sells liability insurance for companies deploying AI agents in production. We scan and red-team the agent workflow, reduce failure modes, and insure the residual risk with purpose-built AI-agent liability coverage. Mount helps companies manage AI risk and unlock AI Agent adoption at scale.**

> “I think this is a great idea. First of all, I’ve been waiting for more people to do this. \[…\] Insurance is shockingly important to how society works. No one is doing a good job of underwriting this right now.” - Sam Altman on Mount

# 

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xo3zVH_pAsc>

# AI Agents Need Insurance

The bottleneck for the economic impact of AI Agents has moved from capability to production-grade reliability and trust. The models are, by far, smart enough for a broad range of use cases, yet many pilot projects are struggling to transition into production.

AI agents now write code, handle customer data, move money, and update records. The more responsibility we give AI systems, the more liability shifts from humans to autonomous systems.

Companies are faced with a simple but impactful question:

“**Who is liable if AI systems fail or cause financial harm**?”

Today, the answer is unclear.

Existing insurance policies are often silent, ambiguous, or exclude autonomous software, simply because they were created many years ago. The insurers behind them don’t want to cover this. They lack the data, the knowledge, and the speed to assess deployed AI systems.

For real production agents, “maybe covered, potentially disputed” is not good enough.

# Why now

Insurance is one of the most heavily regulated industries in existence, creating durable moats that do not shrink even as we progress towards AGI. We are starting now because we believe this market will become obvious in the next 6–12 months:

* Agent adoption is accelerating.
* As agents gain capability, companies give them more responsibility to profit from it.
* Like with any technology, companies will need a risk-transfer mechanism before deploying it in high-stakes workflows.
* Existing cyber and E&O carriers will not want to silently absorb autonomous-agent losses. They do not understand this risk and lack the speed to keep up. We are already seeing a first wave of AI-related exclusions.

# What Mount Does

Today, we’re announcing **Mount AI Agent Liability Insurance**, our first product.

It is designed for mid-market/enterprise companies deploying autonomous AI agents in real business processes.\
Here’s what it does:

1. Scan and red-team the AI deployment.
2. Quantify the operational risk and secure vulnerabilities.
3. Insure residual risk with purpose-built AI liability coverage.

This product delivers peace of mind for thousands of AI-native companies conquering their industries.

# Vision

Mount is best thought of as a highly automated commercial insurance carrier.

Today, commercial insurance runs on manual underwriting, slow pricing, paper-heavy policy issuance, brokers, MGAs, TPAs, claims handlers, and large back-office teams. AI changes that. It allows us to automate underwriting, pricing, issuance, claims, fraud detection, customer support, and distribution from the ground up.

Our first product is AI liability insurance. That is the right wedge because AI risk is new, poorly understood, and difficult for traditional carriers to underwrite. But the bigger vision is not to remain in a single niche. We want to use AI liability as the initial beachhead, build the underwriting and operating infrastructure, and then expand aggressively into additional commercial insurance lines.

The goal is simple: to offer faster, cheaper, and better coverage than incumbents by rebuilding the carrier stack with AI at its core.

# Team

Fabian studied CS/ML at ETH Zürich before dropping out and has been building AI systems for 6+ years. While building his last startup, he saw firsthand how technically performing systems get blocked on their way to production if they can't build trust and prove reliability.

John previously founded an AI-first media company at 18 after dropping out of high school and scaled it to $400K in revenue. Automating every step from intake to fulfillment, he knows what it means to rebuild traditional processes from the ground up.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101822&key=user_uploads/3284831/de838c30-d8d1-4fbf-a56c-7b559c42a561)

---

## Get in touch

If you are deploying AI agents, looking to insure AI-related risks, or interested in investing in the next generation of commercial insurance, we’d love to talk.

launches.body:
### **⚡TL;DR**

**Infera is the Claude Code for scientific instruments.** Describe an experiment in plain English, and Infera turns it into a validated, instrument-ready run, handling the protocol logic, vendor scripts, data, and inventory across the instruments your lab already uses. One system, from intent to execution.

### 🤔 **The Problem**

Labs run on hardware from the future and software from the past.

The instruments are extraordinary. Mass specs identify thousands of proteins, flow cytometers read tens of thousands of cells a second, and cryo-EMs image at near-atomic resolution. These are the machines behind biomarker discovery, immunotherapy, structural biology, and drug development. But the software around them still looks like it shipped in 2003, and runs like it.

We've watched labs running \~6 instruments from 3+ vendors write a one-off script for every experiment, stitch outputs together by hand, and track inventory in a Google Sheet someone probably forgot to update last Tuesday. Scientists spend their week being human glue between machines that should already talk to each other.

### **🔍How Infera Works**

[**Demo Video**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3GPze4X7AeA)

**I. Describe the experiment in plain English.** Infera asks the right questions, surfaces edge cases, and checks against your lab’s inventory and instrument state.

**II. Infera turns it into a run, accommodating both manual and automatable steps.** For programmable instruments, it generates vendor-specific scripts, executes, pulls the data back, and runs the analysis. For manual work like pipetting, gels, hand fermentation, etc., it's the context layer underneath: which step you're on, which reagent goes where, what could go wrong, and how others in the lab have run it before.

**III. The knowledge stays.** Every protocol, every validated run, every edge case becomes part of the system and checked against instrument constraints, lab SOPs, inventory, and prior experiments.

That last part is the hard part. It's what general-purpose LLMs can't do, and it's what enables a researcher to trust the output the way they'd trust a trained technician.

### 👩‍🔬 **Team**

Hi! We’re Chloe and Troy, and we're building Infera to close the gap between science and instrumentation.

* Chloe studied Mechanical Engineering at Harvard. She's been building research software and medical devices since before college (Regeneron STS Scholar), including a microfluidic device that detects harmful chemicals in household products, and has been doing research at places like Fred Hutch, Brigham and Women's, Harvard Medical School, and Pacific Northwest National Lab.
* Troy studied Computation & Neural Systems at Caltech, where he held an endowed research fellowship in a top research lab as an undergraduate. He's published two first-author cancer papers, holds a first-inventor agtech patent, and built and sold two companies before Infera.

Between us, we've run experiments by hand, written the scripts, and watched the whole system break when one person leaves. That's the problem we're building Infera to fix.

### **🎯Ask**

We're currently running pilots with Boston-area academic labs and cores. If any of these are you, reach out at [**hello@infera.bio**](mailto:hello@infera.bio):

* **Academic labs and cores:** know a PI or core director in proteomics, genomics, flow, automation, or screening? We'd love an intro, and we're happy to set up a pilot
* **YC founders with wet labs (diagnostics, therapeutics, synbio, tools):** we’d love to meet whoever runs your lab ops
* **Biotech and life sciences folks:** come say hi
* **Instrument manufacturers** whose customers wish the software were better, let's talk

**TLDR**: we are building a new generation of UUVs (Unmanned Underwater Vehicle) for defense of critical maritime infrastructure.

The evolution of modern battlefields shows the same pattern everywhere: highly expensive military systems are increasingly being challenged by agile, low-cost technologies produced at scale.

In Ukraine, cheap aerial drones have transformed warfare and forced entire defense doctrines to adapt. We think the same shift is about to happen underwater, and are obsessed with the question of what the “drone moment” for underwater warfare would look like.

So we started speaking with submariners, naval operators, ex-commandos, and defense engineers. The demand signal was much stronger than we expected, and the common need is always the same: **cost-effective** and highly **modular** underwater **vehicles** acting in **swarms** that can **adapt quickly** to operational requirements (speed, range, sonar equipment, payloads, etc.). Today, very few solutions exist.

A couple of days after deciding to pivot, we wanted to move as fast as possible and get something real in the water before Demo Day. So we built our **first modular prototype within a week**. It already integrates the main subsystems and was designed to evolve quickly based on operator feedback and mission requirements. Here is a photo:

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102410&key=user_uploads/3424825/4d4a7af2-8dcc-4dac-9ddd-037f9606cdba)

**Our ask:**

Would love to connect with people across the defense ecosystem - especially naval operators, submariners, maritime special operations, and teams working on subsea robotics, maritime autonomy, or distributed naval warfare across Europe, NATO, and allied countries.

launches.body:
Hi there! I’m Gustav, and together with Tine and Marc we’re building AI infrastructure that automates compliance for global retailers.

If you sell physical products across markets, compliance is brutal.

Every country has different requirements. Documentation is fragmented. Regulations change constantly. Most teams still manage it in spreadsheets, consultants, and shared drives. And every product launch becomes a fire drill.

Our users are:

\- Enterprise retailers with thousands of SKUs

\- Compliance, quality, and sourcing teams

\- Companies launching across multiple EU and international markets

They don’t want to just be compliant. They want to ship products fast and never think about compliance again.

**How we got here**

Just one month after Tine and I met back in May 2024, we made a deal with Flying Tiger Copenhagen (a 1,000+ store global retail chain, similar to a European Five Below) and forward deployed ourselves in their offices, working directly with their compliance, packaging, and sourcing teams for over a year.

We had no idea how much manual work we were about to witness.

Regulations are dynamic. Products change. Data is messy. Requirements depend on category, market, material, packaging, claims, and more. Most existing tools treat compliance like static storage.

So we built an AI-native system that:

\- Maps products to relevant regulatory requirements across markets

\- Transforms messy product data into structured, audit-ready compliance records

\- Automatically generates legally required outputs — including translations, warnings, labels, risk assessments, declarations, and technical documentation

\- Propagates updates when regulations or products change, so documentation stays compliant without manual rework

Today we manage 100k+ products, work with large retailers across Europe, and are growing \~45% MoM

If you know large retailers selling across markets, tell them they can save millions in yearly compliance costs - while launching more products in more markets, faster.

And if you’re building or operating in retail, import/export, or compliance infrastructure, we’d love to compare notes!

Demo: [**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4omoq7tcU88**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4omoq7tcU88)

Today, drug and device companies outsource clinical operations to legacy CROs and their massive teams, which is why the CRO market is $82B annually. Harbor delivers the regulated services companies buy from legacy CROs, but built around our AI-native system of record from day one. Our software already automates the core data workflows: study build, data capture, query generation, monitoring, signing, and database lock. Because we own the system of record, we can expand into the surrounding service workflows: site contracting and billing, subject engagement and retention, statistics, reporting, and more.

We built Harbor because we lived through the problem.
