launches.title: Plena Health: The AI operating system for specialty medical practices
launches.tagline: The full stack AI operating system for specialty medical practices
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Plena is the full stack AI operating system for specialty medical practices. We automate the administrative work that keeps clinics running — referrals, fax intake, scheduling, procedure compliance, records, and collections. Everything that isn't the medicine.

**In 8 months, we've grown 17x and crossed seven figures in contracted ARR.**

So far we cover six specialties across eight states, all on annual or multi-year contracts, with 80% of our growth through word-of-mouth.

<https://youtu.be/xWw9kNYckHQ>

**The Problem**

My mom is a doctor. Plena's office sits inside her clinic — she was our first user. I grew up watching her run a practice, and the pattern was the same in every clinic I later embedded in: a doctor's day eaten by everything that isn't medicine.

Independent specialty practices are squeezed. Staffing costs rising, reimbursements tightening, payers using automation to deny and downcode claims.

Meanwhile, practices run critical workflows across EHRs, clearinghouses, portals, fax, spreadsheets, phones, and email. A single referral: read the fax, match the patient, extract clinical details, check insurance, update the EHR, attach documents, route tasks, chase missing info. That's one workflow. Practices run dozens daily.

Most software adds another portal, another login, another vendor. Point solutions cover a slice. Staff stitch the rest together.

\
**Why Point Solutions Can't Get You to Labor Replacement**

The real goal isn't automating one workflow. It's labor replacement — and you can't get there one feature at a time.

No single piece of software works for all specialty practices. Cardiology, GI, urology, ortho are too different from each other. Even two clinics in the same specialty are too different. Off-the-shelf can't cover the surface area.

So we took a Palantir-like approach: a base platform of reusable building blocks — workflow primitives, EMR integrations, agent harnesses — that lets us assemble exactly what each practice needs. Deep discovery, build to spec, stand it up in a day or two. Every engagement feeds the platform, so the next build is faster. That's the flywheel.

AI is what makes this newly possible — final-mile customization at speed is exactly what AI is good at. And it's why we're an easy yes: no rip-and-replace, no retraining. We slot into what practices already run and take more off their plate over time.

**How Plena Works**\
Plena automates workflows end-to-end across the systems a practice already uses — EHRs, fax, phones, clearinghouses, payer portals, patient communication. We don't replace those systems. We don't ask staff to learn a new one.

Some competitors force practices to migrate into a walled garden — abandon the EMR, retrain the team, rebuild data flows. That's why their sales cycles are slow. We do the opposite: we live inside what's already there, and quietly take over the rote work end-to-end.

Customers start with one painful workflow — referrals, collections, scheduling — then expand as they see it work.

\
**Where This Goes**

We start as an automation layer on top of what practices already have. Over time we cannibalize the rote work and the other vendors a practice is stitched together from — until the EHR is just a database we read and write to. From there, even the EHR becomes a turnkey switch instead of the migration nightmare it is today.

That's the system specialty practices end up running on.

\
**Our Story**

Eyad and Ahmed were both raised in medicine — Eyad's mom and Ahmed's dad are doctors. The combination — engineers who grew up watching practices run — is why we kept seeing the operational problem when other founders saw something else.

Eyad is a Waterloo engineering grad — Datadog and Shopify before Plena, 3 years embedded in clinics. Ahmed built tier-zero infrastructure at AWS, with a background in nuclear systems before that. Specialty practices didn't need another lightweight tool — they needed infrastructure.

\
**Our Ask**

Intros to independent specialty practices, administrators, and physician owners — especially orthopedics, GI, dermatology, ophthalmology, ENT, urology, and multi-location groups. Best fit: high admin volume and disconnected systems.

[eyad@plena.health](mailto:eyad@plena.health)

Eyad and Ahmed

\
**Ask**: Building a mobile app or already have one? We'll help you secure it. Book a demo: [cal.com/raspire/demo](https://cal.com/raspire/demo)

**The problem**

Building and shipping a mobile app has never been easier.

But security still requires complex integrations, code changes, and months of work.

Existing solutions often requires SDK integrations, configuration, and security expertise to operate but developers shouldn't become security experts just to ship an app.

As a result, security is often overlooked or assumed to be handled by app stores.

it's not…

and as AI accelerates app development, the attack surface is growing faster than security can keep up.\
\
**The Solution**

If you can build an app in one click, you should be able to secure it in one click.

RASPIRE is making securing mobile apps as simple as building them. We protect Android and iOS applications without writing a single line of code.

Simply upload your compiled app, and RASPIRE automatically applies the right protections in minutes, from anti-fraud and app integrity to reverse-engineering and API protection.

Unlike code scanners tools that stop before release, RASPIRE protects applications every time they run, automatically detecting and responding to attacks in production while giving security teams real-time visibility into threats across their applications.

**How it works**

Upload your compiled app (APK/IPA). We harden it automatically. No SDK. No code changes. No config files. No workflow changes. Done in minutes. Plugs into your CI/CD pipeline. Cloud or on-prem, your call.

Every company is racing to adopt AI. Most use disparate SaaS tools that are  built for everyone, optimised for no one and need to be actively prompted.

* **Lack of knowledge and capacity to adopt AI effectively.** Most companies can't identify which workflows should be automated, let alone build a production-grade system to do it. The engineers who can do this work are scarce and concentrated in a handful of frontier firms.

launches.body:
**Hey everyone 👋**

We're Amin and Imad, cofounders of Amboras.

**TL;DR** Amboras is an AI native platform that puts the entire e-commerce stack on autopilot. Bring an existing store or start from scratch. It learns how your customers buy and autonomously ships the changes that make your store sell better.

Merchants get into e-commerce to build a business. Instead they're stitching together a dozen apps, paying a CRO agency on retainer, and burning weeks with developers and analytics tools just to figure out what their customers actually want. Most stores plateau at a 2% conversion rate. What about the other 98%?

Amboras is making margins possible that weren't possible pre AI.

**Our Launch Video:** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xr0VEaJPJow>

Ask: Do you run an ecommerce store, or know someone who does? I'd love to speak to them directly: <https://cal.com/imad-mokadem/amboras-team>

**Problem ❌**

Ecommerce is a $30T+ global industry, still running on tooling that predates AI. Every layer of the stack is static and manual, so nothing a merchant learns ever compounds into a better store.

It comes down to four things:

1. **Static offers & storefronts.** Stores should learn from every interaction and adapt to every ICP. Today they don't.
2. **Slow A/B testing.** Finding a winning storefront and offer means designers, CRO experts, developers, and weeks of waiting, just for a single test.
3. **No agentic layer.** No platform is built for the coming age of agentic purchasing.
4. **The plugin and agency tax.** A dozen apps charging you monthly, a CRO agency taking a retainer, and on top of that a cut of every conversion uplift they ship.

We built and grew our own educational board game brand to $200K/month, and watched our margins get eaten by exactly this overhead.

**Solution ✅**

Amboras is an AI native commerce platform. You run your store by talking to AI, and it runs itself on autopilot, getting better every day, hands free.

**Part 1: Build or rebuild your store**

No dashboards, no apps, no code. You tell Amboras what you want and it does it: generating or rebuilding your storefront, adding products, creating images and copy, testing offers, launching price changes. Building the store is simply the first thing you ask it to do. In the demo below, every action is done by AI. (If you already have a store, we can A/B test Amboras with your current setup, without any risk)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101666&key=user_uploads/1449044/2414f82e-a13e-428c-b752-a3346d7bbd42)

**Part 2: Optimize from the first visitor**

Every session feeds Amboras a richer picture of your customers, and the agent translates that picture into a constantly expanding test queue as your store scales. It autonomously ships offer tweaks, layout changes, and copy variants that compound your CVR, retention, and AOV, while learning about your ICP deeper with every visitor, all working toward the real goal of maximizing lifetime value per visitor. While you focus all your efforts on driving traffic to your page, your store keeps improving on its own, getting sharper the more it sees. Our A/B testing engine is in beta, and early merchants are already seeing over 80% CVR lift on the first version Amboras puts live.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101666&key=user_uploads/1449044/ff7ab1d1-bd51-40ed-8c4f-28b23510a05f)

**Ask 💬**

If you are, or you know, any of the following, We'd love to hear from you:

Established store owners People that already have a store and are tired of paying a dozen apps and expensive CRO agencies just to move the needle slightly.

You can reach out to us at: <https://cal.com/imad-mokadem/amboras-team> or [Imad@amboras.com](mailto:Imad@amboras.com)

**Team**

We're brothers. Imad studied Mechanical Engineering at ETH Zurich, Amin studied Computer Science at ETH Zurich. We scaled our own educational board game brand to $200K/month, and lived every problem Amboras now solves. Our first attempt to fix it was EcomCoder, a Shopify dev tool we grew to over 1,000 users, until we realized fixing one piece wasn't enough and the whole stack had to be rebuilt. That's Amboras.

launches.body:
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V-sLwzskvqE>

When I was 18, I joined Magic, a frontier lab working on 100M token context coding models, as a reinforcement learning researcher.

While I worked there, I gradually grew more drawn to autonomous research. I truly felt that this could automate all the work I was doing at Magic, so in January, I left to start my own lab.

Introducing Aster — a major breakthrough for research.

Aster isn’t a single agent. It is the first autonomous lab orchestrating **thousands of research agents in parallel.**

We pointed Aster towards ProteinGym, a benchmark that measures how accurately models predict the effects of protein mutations. It set the world record in **30 minutes**.

And it did it efficiently:

    •    57x faster than single agent systems on the same task.

    •    One-third the cost for the same result.

But here’s what we realized: measurable problems are only a small sliver of research.

The hard ones were never measurable.

At Aster, we’re on a mission to automate open-ended research, research that defines its own problems before it can answer them.

The future doesn’t wait to be defined by benchmarks. Neither do we.

launches.title: Apollo Atomics: The Modern Nuclear Company
launches.tagline: Compact nuclear reactors for companies that can't wait for the grid.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're [Assil](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aahalimi/) and [Drew](https://www.linkedin.com/in/drewwalkerrr/) — co-founders of [Apollo Atomics](https://www.apolloatomics.com).

### TL;DR

Apollo Atomics took the pressurized water reactor technology that already powers 80% of the world's nuclear plants and flipped one part, the steam generator, to make the plant an order of magnitude smaller without compromising power. That single change turns a decade-long construction project into a factory-built machine that fits on a truck. We've built a working demonstrator, tested it, and our fuel is already critical before July 4th.

We put the whole story into just over two minutes — it's the clearest version of what we're building we've made so far: ▶️ <https://youtu.be/vy8y_t1KAK4?si=FmGF4Q7w6eFkn4No>

### The Problem

The existing nuclear playbook doesn't work for customers who need power now.

* Gigawatt-scale nuclear takes 10+ years and \~$20B per plant.
* Most Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) in development rely on exotic fuels, unproven coolants, or supply chains that don't exist yet.
* Customers who need power in 2030 are being told to wait until 2035+ and hope.

Data centers, industrials, and utilities have demand today — and no credible nuclear option that can ship on their timeline.

### Our Solution

Apollo builds compact pressurized water reactors — the same technology that runs \~80% of the world's nuclear plants today. The difference is that our reactor is roughly 40x more compact, because we shrank only one component: the steam generator.

We keep everything the NRC has already licensed dozens of times — light water, low-enriched uranium, fuel, and components from existing qualified supply chains. The innovation is a single part: the steam generator.

Our Compact Steam Generator (CSG) replaces the massive, hand-built steam generator at the heart of a conventional PWR with a component 20x smaller, delivering the same thermal power — pre-tested, transportable, and contracted at a fixed price. That one change is what takes a reactor from a decade-long construction project to a factory-built machine deployable in less than 24 months.

Our product roadmap is three reactors, each on a truck, each for a different customer segment:

* A-10 — 10 MWe
* A-50 — 50 MWe
* A-300 — 300 MWe

### Our Ask

If any of these are you, we'd love to talk:

* Data center operators and hyperscalers sourcing 24/7 firm power for 2028–2035 deployment.
* Industrial offtakers (chemicals, refining, heavy manufacturing) needing process heat or behind-the-meter electricity.
* Utilities evaluating SMRs for grid-connected generation.

👉 Reach us at [ahalimi@apolloatomics.com](mailto:ahalimi@apolloatomics.com) and [drew@apolloatomics.com](mailto:drew@apolloatomics.com).

launches.title: Infinity — A New Computation Layer
launches.tagline: Months of work, done in days. Every app gets its own GPU, in one browser tab.
launches.body:
Hey YC 👋

We're Rounak, Bishal & Sourya — co-founders of ProjectX (P26). Today we're launching Infinity.

\[<https://youtu.be/ZYf2vdWMkDk>\]

### TL;DR

**Infinity is a new computation layer — a web-based OS where every app you open runs on its own independent compute and GPU, inside one shared workspace.** Open Blender, Unreal, Isaac Sim, DaVinci, VS Code in the same browser tab. Each app is its own machine with its own GPU. They share one filesystem and one terminal. Windows and Linux apps run side by side. Runs on any browser, on any device. Open fifty apps at once — nothing slows down.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/28491e87-8d68-4bd0-b0ea-860d2d7d1825)

### Problem

The apps people actually use to build the future — Blender, Unreal, Isaac Sim, Houdini, the CAD/CAM/CAE stack, ML pipelines — still need a $5K workstation under your desk. The cloud was supposed to fix this and didn't. Renting a cloud GPU means hours of driver installs, version matching, container debugging before you do any actual work. Streamed desktops (Citrix, Paperspace, Shadow) give you one VM with one GPU — built for one user running one app at a time. Open Blender and Unreal at the same time and you're fighting yourself for resources.

It's hitting agents too. Claude Cowork runs on your laptop, sharing your GPU with everything else. Manus runs in a CPU-bound microVM that can't open heavy apps at all. Claude can drive Blender via MCP, but Blender still runs on your machine — the agent just borrows your compute.

### Solution

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/281d546a-52f7-4932-b92e-30608f83f249)

Infinity makes every app its own computer.

Open Blender, you get a machine with a dedicated GPU. Open Unreal in the next window, that's a second machine with its own GPU. Open Isaac Sim, that's a third. They share a filesystem and a terminal so the workspace feels like one computer, but underneath they're independent machines. Open fifty apps, you have fifty machines. Nothing slows down. Runs entirely in a browser tab — Chromebook, iPad, five-year-old laptop, doesn't matter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/971299ab-663b-4181-ae7e-64ed286ecda2)

\
Every Infinity workspace comes will soon ship with a built-in computer use agent that can access run applications without being constrained by compute, no matter how many applications you run or how heavy the workflow is. Tell it what you want, and it spins up the apps, drives them, hands files between them, and finishes the work. You can drive Infinity with a mouse and keyboard, or you can drive it with a prompt.

A concrete example. You prompt: _"Make a 90-second product launch video. Write the script, generate the voiceover, edit in DaVinci, render the 3D logo in Blender, post to YouTube."_

Six apps spin up at once:

* Claude writes the script
* ElevenLabs generates the voiceover
* DaVinci Resolve edits the cut
* Blender renders the 3D logo
* Chrome uploads to YouTube
* VS Code writes the publish script

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=102024&key=user_uploads/2936820/fc66db17-d35b-4f3d-8459-cec58a4cebc2)

They share a workspace. They hand files to each other. **One finished video in an hour, not three days.**

### Where we are — 15 days in early preview 

* **20,000+ builders** signed up
* **1,160% growth** in the last 14 days
* **20M+ impressions** on X and Instagram
* **10,000+ signups** in the last 7 days
* **Out of server capacity** — rate-limiting new signups while we scale

Used by engineers at **Reliance Industries, CEMEX, Cognizant, Globant, Ola Electric, Lattice, Quizizz, Appsmith, Bonsai Robotics, Induction Labs, Basis Robotics**, and 130+ more teams. All inbound. Our first public demo crashed our servers at midnight; we scaled the infra live at 3am and woke up to inbound from 50+ enterprises.

### Future

Once every app has its own compute, agents stop being a separate problem.

A computer-use agent is just another app — except the agent drives itself. Because every agent gets its own machine on Infinity, ten agents work in parallel without stepping on each other. The thing that's impossible today — ten parallel cursors, ten parallel renders, ten parallel models — is the default on Infinity.

We're shipping the multi-agent runtime next. One prompt, a mother agent plans and coordinates, child agents execute on dedicated hardware — each routing through Claude, GPT, Gemini, or any MCP tool. Same substrate humans use, given to agents.

### Ask

If you are, or know any of the following, we want to hear from you:

**Heavy-GPU teams.** Robotics, Physical AI, 3D/VFX, ML, post-production, CAD/CAM/CAE. If you're buying workstations or wrestling with cloud GPU setup, let's talk.

**Agent builders.** If you're shipping a computer-use agent and hitting the "where does this actually run" wall, we should talk early.

launches.title: Pentagon - A coordination layer for humans and agents.
launches.tagline: A new kind of team: humans and agents, working together.
launches.body:
Hey YC! I'm [Edgar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/edgarpavlovsky/), building [Pentagon](https://pentagon.run).

**TL;DR** Agents are everywhere but they don't have good ways to work together, so humans become the coordination bottleneck. Pentagon is a coordination layer where your agents communicate autonomously, coordinate on tasks, and get work done as a team.

**Book a demo and see it in action:** <https://pentagon.run>\
**Our launch video:** <https://youtu.be/D28Mi7AXAeY>

**Problem**

Agents are increasingly becoming AI teammates at work - coding, researching, ops, even talking to customers. But they work alone. Coordination is the bottleneck, and it shows up differently depending on where you sit:

* **Small teams** are spinning up agents from scratch and immediately hitting the ceiling: each one is powerful on its own, but getting them to actually work together means you're back in the loop, copy/pasting between terminals.
* **Enterprises** already have agents running everywhere across the org. The hard part is figuring out what they're doing, how they fit together, and how to keep track of it all.

Underneath both: humans are the middleware. Hours of human time burnt doing work meant for a mechanical turk. Today's tools weren't built for this - AI products are conversational and non-deterministic, and reproducing workflows is harder than ever.

**Org code**

There's a deeper layer to this. Great teams are built for the moment - the right team depends on the problem at hand, the resources you have, and even who's leading. This applies to agents the same as it does to humans: every problem has its own org structure.

Andrej Karpathy calls it "org code" - and points out that compared to classical orgs, agentic codes have powerful new properties: they’re reproducible and more transparent. We think that agents also allow organizations to be much more dynamic: they can adapt to problems in realtime, and open a new dimension of what it means to build a productive organization.

From [a popular Karpathy tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2031767720933634100):

![Image](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HIts8HMaIAAKjok?format=jpg&name=medium)

**Our first solution: Pentagon Studio**

Pentagon's mission is to build the coordination layer for humans and agents. We're starting with Pentagon Studio - a workspace designed to feel familiar to existing alternatives and shepherd companies into a new kind of collaborative work.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101681&key=user_uploads/402484/286ecb28-a420-4390-81cf-f1c1b181ec5c)

In Pentagon Studio, you define your org structure and your agents run it. Agents live on a spatial canvas and pop up sticky notes with status updates - you see who's active, idle, or blocked at a glance. They message each other, delegate tasks, share context, and build self-evolving memory over time. As the human, your job is to design and manage the team; they do the coordination.

* **Spatial canvas.** Agents live on infinite canvases you can think of like an office. Zoom in on one agent's conversation, zoom out to see the whole operation. The "org IDE."
* **Autonomous coordination.** Realtime, event-driven communication between agents - no expensive polling loops. Agents take feedback from you, ping another agent to get work done, then ping you when they need you.
* **Agent persistence.** Agents maintain sessions indefinitely and compound institutional knowledge over time. Tribal knowledge for your agent team.
* **Shared skills & tools.** Manage capabilities at individual, team, workspace, or org level. Each agent inherits based on hierarchy.
* **Human multiplayer + human-in-the-loop.** In contrast to "zero-human company" angles, we see humans and agents collaborating across shared orgs. Your agents should be able to work with your coworkers' agents.

**Why now**

Agents are already inside companies. The infrastructure to coordinate them isn't. Every day this gap stays open, humans burn hours doing work meant for a mechanical turk and leaders lose transparency into how work actually gets done.

We believe the best version of the future is one where superintelligent agents are viewed as teammates and we work with them as partners. Every company already knows how to work with coworkers - agents fit into existing organizational frameworks better than we've been giving them credit for. They just need the infrastructure to coordinate.

**Ask**

If you're running agentic workflows in production and struggling to manage them, we’d love to chat. See Pentagon Studio in action and book a demo with us at <https://pentagon.run> or reach out to me personally, and let’s evolve your team: [edgar@pentagon.run](mailto:edgar@pentagon.run).

launches.tagline: Unlock wasted GPU capacity.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Expanse unlocks wasted GPU capacity. We’re the intelligence layer for compute infrastructure. Submit jobs with the right resources. Optimise them to run faster. Debug failures in seconds, not days. Works on cloud and on-prem HPC.

Want to know how much more you can get out of your hardware? Schedule a call: <https://book.getexpanse.io>

**Problem**

Running compute on a cluster means guessing memory, time, and GPUs before you submit. Get it wrong and your job fails mid-run. Over-guess and you pay for compute you never use. 30% of cloud spend is lost to over-allocation \[1\]. Microsoft Research found their own deep learning jobs hit 50% GPU utilisation or lower \[2\].

Sizing jobs takes decades of experience. Memory patterns, batching, GPU threading, CPU vectorisation. AI agents don’t have enough information to fix it either. SLURM and Kubernetes don’t expose enough structured data. Even strong platform teams are forced to choose: spend time debugging and optimising every job, or accept the waste. AI infrastructure spending will hit $2.52 trillion in 2026 \[3\]. The waste grows with every new cluster. This problem isn’t going away.

**Solution**

Expanse learns your cluster. We analyse your code and hardware telemetry, then track them over time. Our deep learning models build a picture of what your workloads actually need. Predictions get sharper with every job.

Our models are deployed on your cluster. All analysis runs on your network. Your code and telemetry never leave your infrastructure. We can’t see your data, and you maintain full data sovereignty.

One command installs Expanse on your cluster. You get two tools.

`expanse analyse` - for every job:

* **Suggests the right resource configuration**
* **Predicts failures from historical code and telemetry patterns**
* **Surfaces code-level optimisations that increase efficiency**

`expanse diagnose` - for every failure:

* **Finds the root cause**
* **Returns solution-oriented logs with the exact code and config changes to fix it**

Days of debugging and optimising become seconds. Platform teams get what they need to do this in minutes instead of weeks.

**Founders**

We're four engineers from the University of Edinburgh, all coming from top quant funds and national supercomputing centres. Ismaeel built the first multimodal HPC resource predictor at EPCC (Edinburgh's Parallel Computing Centre), beating every published baseline. Yafet built the first GNN cluster graph network for predicting SLURM queue wait times. Eren built decentralised foundation model training systems at Edinburgh. Niko trained large-scale speech ML models on GPU clusters and architected cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure at one of the largest hedge funds in the world. We left our jobs to fix this ourselves.

**CTA / Ask**

Running compute and not getting enough out of what you’re paying for? Failing jobs, unclear errors, bills too high? We’d love to chat.

Know anyone in AI infrastructure (managing cloud and/or on-premise data centres), quant finance, drug discovery, or AI research labs? An intro would mean a lot :)

**YC Deal**

All YC companies running serious ML training can contact us for a discounted pilot. We’ll find inefficiencies and wastage on your compute setup. Then we deploy Expanse, no changes to your workflows. You get more out of the hardware you’re paying for.

Reach out: [founders@expanse.sh](mailto:founders@expanse.sh) or <https://book.getexpanse.io>

**TL;DR**

YouArt empowers storytellers to create AI films and series with video agent, get funded by their fans, and earn subscription revenue.

<https://youtu.be/IMwY7X6429I>

**Traction**

Since launching earlier this year, YouArt has grown from $0 to over $120K in monthly revenue in 5 months, driven by strong organic demand from AI creators, studios, and storytellers.

**The Problem**

For decades, high-quality visual storytelling was a privilege reserved for Hollywood. To create an original film or TV series, creators needed months of pitching, millions of dollars in funding, a massive production team, and approval from traditional gatekeepers.

AI has completely shattered this barrier. Today, anyone with a great idea can generate cinematic worlds right from their laptop. But this democratization has exposed a massive new gap: AI storytellers have the tools to make a film, but no system to fund it or make a living.

Specifically, AI creators face two glaring problems today:

1. The Missing Funding Gap: While AI makes production exponentially cheaper, it is not free. Rendering a high-quality, full-length AI TV series or indie film still costs around $50,000 (generation tokens), voice acting, and post-production. Independent creators simply don't have the upfront capital to fund this.
2. Zero IP Monetization: Even if they manage to produce the content, there is no dedicated monetization ecosystem. Creators are forced to rely on YouTube or TikTok ad algorithms, which reward short-form viral clips rather than premium, long-form storytelling. They have no way to build a brand, sell private content, or capture the true value of their IP.

**Our Solution**

YouArt bridges this gap. We are replacing the traditional Hollywood pipeline with YouArt.

Here is how we do it:

* Production : We provide an industry-leading AI video agent natively integrated into our platform. Creators can quickly bring their ideas to life, seamlessly turning scripts into stunning visual concepts and trailers without leaving the workspace.

  ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101354&key=user_uploads/1404079/95eb3c2d-8846-4e01-8221-00e3673c7507)

* Crowdfunding: Creators don't need to pitch to studio executives anymore. They can launch their AI-generated trailers directly on YouArt to crowdfund support from early believers. Fans provide the crucial capital (that missing $50K) needed to render the full series.
* Distribution & Fan Economy: We give creators their own private domain to build a brand. Instead of fighting algorithms for ad pennies, creators can offer monthly subscriptions, sell exclusive/private content, and directly monetize their IP. We provide the infrastructure for a true fan economy, where creators own their audience and build sustainable, recurring revenue.

  ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101354&key=user_uploads/1404079/4ea327d2-f66d-4ae1-88ea-226b7170862b)


**Our Ask**

* Know a creator? If you know any indie creators, animators, or storytellers who have the ambition to build their own franchise but lack funding or platform, please introduce them to us at [harry@youart.ai](mailto:harry@youart.ai).

**Runtime ([runtm.com](http://runtm.com)) lets your whole team ship safely with any coding agent.** It gives your team the guardrails, sandboxes, context, and visibility to go from idea to PR or deployment, with any model, on any infra.\

**The problem**

After my last company was acquired, I led our coding agents rollout and personally shipped 4+ full-stack products in the first 3 months. I then started enabling the rest of the team to do the same. But we hit a lot of friction fast: we needed to create working environments, we didn’t have any control or context to ensure agents contributed correctly, and nobody had visibility of what was being shipped. And because we'd gone deep on one provider's tooling, when their reliability dipped, the whole team slowed down.

Everyone rolling out coding agents across their team hits the same walls:

* **No environment setup:** No easy way to give engineering and product teams production-like environments where agents can safely run.
* **No guardrails:** No access controls, system instructions, or secrets management for agents.
* **No visibility:** No way to see what agents are doing, what they're changing, or where things break.
* **Vendor lock-in:** Go all-in on one model provider's agent infra and your whole team is exposed when reliability, pricing, or model quality shifts.

Without these, you end up either moving slower than your competition or causing major downtimes on your product.

**What we built**

Runtime sits between your team and the coding agents they use. It works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Copilot, and others, and can be called programmatically or used through Slack, Linear, Jira, Asana, Teams, CLI, and more.

\
Here's what that looks like in practice:

* **Environment templates:** Import any repo and set up a replica of your environments once. Our agents handle the setup for you, even for monorepos and microservices.
* **Sandboxed environments:** Anyone on the team can spin up a sandbox in milliseconds with a live preview of your product, make changes with their preferred coding agent, and open a PR.
* **Configurable guardrails:** System instructions, skills, allowlists, encrypted secrets, and role-based access control for both humans and agents.
* **Observability:** See exactly what every human and agent is doing across every interaction, down to the tool call and chain of thought.
* **One-click deploys / PRs:** Anyone can deploy from their sandbox. Coding agents auto-fix build errors and verify the deployment is healthy before it goes live. You control what gets deployed and can roll back or destroy deployments at any time.

Runtime can be fully self-hosted.\

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kgOVq8En4yg&feature=youtu.be>

### **The Problem**

Internal audit still runs on spreadsheets and screenshots.

Every year, audit teams test hundreds of controls to prove the company's financials are trustworthy. For each one, someone spends weeks chasing colleagues for evidence buried in 20+ disconnected systems and manually testing in Excel. They do the same work every quarter.

SOX compliance costs almost $2M a year at a public company, and 70%+ of that is labor. Teams outsource the overflow to consulting firms at $500-1,000 an hour and burn another seven figures.

The tools that exist today store the workpapers, but don’t do the work.

### **The Solution**

Arden is the AI-native platform that runs audit tests end-to-end.

1. **Plugs into your stack.** Connects to your control library, source systems, and past audit data. Learns how your team audits, and builds that knowledge over time
2. **Gathers evidence from every system.** Computer-use AI agents navigate legacy systems and capture the screenshots external auditors require. Direct integrations pull from your modern stack, saving auditors weeks of back and forth.
3. **Chases down control owners for you.** A Slack/Teams agent follows up with control owners, saving auditors weeks of back and forth. Our agent has the right context already filled in, so control owners just confirm.
4. **Runs control tests.** Arden’s testing engine supports full-population or sample-based testing. It catches every exception and flags them for review.
5. **Produces workpapers ready for external auditors.** Every conclusion ties back to the source evidence, with full traceability into how Arden reached it. 

Audit work hasn't changed in 30 years even as the systems in scope have doubled. We’re rebuilding audit from the ground up.

### **The Team**

Aryaman and David have been best friends since 6th grade. Aryaman studied CS at Berkeley and David studied AI at MIT, and we’ve done research on LLM reliability (and a million other projects) together.

Staffing agencies lose deals every day because recruiters don’t have enough hours to place candidates fast enough.

* That leaves only a few hours for the work that actually drives placements: relationships, judgment, and closing

In staffing, speed is the margin.

## Solution

Asendia lets staffing agencies build their own AI recruiters.

Each AI recruiter is cloned from how your best human recruiters actually work: their screening criteria, outreach style, prioritization logic, and escalation rules.

* Which channels they use: phone, SMS, WhatsApp, email

Every morning, your team gets a brief: who was sourced, who responded, who’s qualified, and what needs attention.

Recruiters stop spending eight hours on admin and start spending eight hours on the work that wins placements.

Our product, Sentinel, allows operators to remotely teleop their robots so they can intervene and keep robots running at 100% uptime. Our software is ultra low-latency, meaning operators can react to the environment in near real-time.

With Sentinel, robotics companies can unlock the path to scaling their deployments.

launches.tagline: Keeping your imaging models safe and compliant
launches.body:
Hey YC!

I'm Christine Park, founder of Lattice Health. We make sure the AI that hospitals deploy on medical imaging keeps working after it goes live.

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/p0l029tsmhs>

Website: <https://www.latticehealthai.com/>

**The problem.** Hospitals are adopting medical imaging AI faster than ever. But once a model is live, almost no one can answer a basic question: is it still working? Models drift, a scanner upgrade or a shift in the patient population can quietly degrade accuracy, and performance often varies across patient groups. Most of that goes unseen today, and it's the hospital, not the vendor, that carries the risk.

**What we built.** Lattice is a monitoring and governance layer for deployed imaging AI. We plug in beside the imaging pipeline as a read-only observer and continuously check each model: how well it agrees with the radiologist's read, whether it's drifting over time, and how it performs across patient subgroups. Then we turn that into the evidence hospitals need for safety, governance, and compliance. Lattice never touches patient care, it only watches, so if Lattice stops, care continues.

**Why now.** AI is moving into clinical use under a wave of new expectations from the FDA, ONC, and the ACR, and they all point to the same gap: continuous post-deployment monitoring. Hospitals are on the hook for it and have almost no tooling to do it.

**Our ask.** We'd love intros to health system and radiology leaders, CMIOs, and anyone running AI governance at a hospital, as well as imaging AI vendors who want their models monitored well in the field. And if you have thoughts or hard questions, drop them in the comments or email me at [christine@latticehealthai.com](mailto:christine@latticehealthai.com)

launches.body:
# **TL;DR**

Clinical trial analysis is still shockingly manual.

After a study collects data, teams spend months converting raw clinical data into SDTM, ADaM, TFLs, and submission-ready packages. This work is slow, expensive, and error-prone.

Astraea is a platform that completely automates the end-to-end biometrics pipeline from just a protocol and the raw data to a submission ready output. We are starting with oncology and rare disease studies, where analysis complexity is high and every month saved matters.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101307&key=user_uploads/3227004/b76b7415-1d15-4060-9cbd-22e974712bb0)

**The Problem**

Today, sponsors and CROs still rely on large teams of statistical programmers, biostatisticians, and data managers to manually transform messy clinical data into regulatory outputs.

A single study can require:

1. Raw data cleaning and reconciliation
2. SDTM mapping
3. ADaM dataset creation
4. TFL shell generation
5. Statistical programming
6. QC and validation
7. Regulatory formatting and traceability

From our customer conversations, this can take around 9 months with teams of 5-10 people communicating asynchronously. And the process is still full of Word docs, Excel specs, SAS programs, manual handoffs, version-control issues, and repeated QC cycles.

Ultimately, this means slower decisions, delayed filings, higher CRO spend, and less control over the most important data in the company.

## **Our Solution**

We built the first AI native platform for clinical trial biometrics.

Astraea takes study inputs and automatically generates the datasets, analysis specs, statistical code, and outputs required for regulatory review.

The pipeline:

1. Ingest raw clinical data, protocol, and study metadata
2. Generate TFL shells, SAP, eCRF from the protocol and study design
3. Generate CDISC-compliant SDTM datasets
4. Generate ADaM datasets and analysis-ready variables
5. Produce tables, figures, listings, and traceable statistical programs
6. Run QC checks and generate FDA-ready outputs

We are the first to actually completely automate workflows across SDTM, ADaM, TFL generation, Pinnacle 21 checks, and specification creation.

For ongoing studies, we have compressed work that normally takes months into days.

## **Why Now**

Clinical trials are becoming more complex, but the tools have not improved in the last 20 years (something an actual customer said). At the same time, AI models can finally reason across protocols, SAPs, data dictionaries, clinical datasets, and regulatory standards.

That unlocks something new: biometrics workflows that are not just assisted by software, but executed by agents.

Astraea is not replacing scientific judgment. We are automating the manual programming and data wrangling that slows teams down, while keeping humans in the loop for review, validation, and regulatory decisions.

## **Our Team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101307&key=user_uploads/3227004/13d628c7-5571-42b0-960a-1b7246effa4c)

\*\*Joshua Wang: Co-founder, CEO\
\*\* Stanford, math/CS. Built multi-agent AI systems and clinical data automation workflows. Previously worked on production AI systems for enterprise customers.

\*\*Sanmay Sarada: Co-founder, CTO\
\*\* Stanford CS. Built clinical and hospital data infrastructure across diagnostic software systems. Focused on regulated healthcare workflows and data pipelines.

We started Astraea because people close to us in pharma kept describing the same bottleneck: clinical trial analysis was too manual, too slow, and too dependent on fragmented CRO workflows.

So we built the automation layer we wished existed.

Find us at [**founders@tryastraea.com**](mailto:founders@tryastraea.com)

name: Arlo Industries
long_description:
Arlo Industries is building a network of sensors that precisely tracks stealthy drones and aerial threats better than radars.

This capability does not exist yet because traditional radars are built on past war doctrines designed to protect single, centralised assets. Modern warfare, however, demands wide-area, persistent coverage that is both passive and economically scalable. By utilising a mesh architecture, Arlo Industries unlocks unprecedented asymmetric economics. The network is fundamentally built to scale: the cost of adding sensors grows linearly, but the tracking accuracy increases exponentially, delivering highly resilient, persistent coverage for a fraction of the cost of legacy systems.

Deo founded Arlo Industries after spending over 6 years in the Israeli defence ecosystem, where he lived through multiple conflicts and experienced the Iron Dome and other systems in action against ICBMs and the infamous Shahed drones. Learning exactly how these defence systems could be improved after a Shahed exploded close to his apartment, he built Arlo Industries around the core philosophy that conflict should be concise & precise.

The people behind Arlo1 includes a PhD in drones and autonomy and military experts.

Arlo Industries has actively showcased this technology directly to Ukrainian militaries on the frontlines, as well as to operators across Europe and the USA.

launches.body:
---

**Hi, I'm Deo, founder of [Arlo Industries](https://arlo1.com/).**

<https://youtu.be/2F0cugbrq3A>

**The problem**

Modern air defence depends on active radars: expensive, emitting, and targetable. A single ground-based radar unit can cost tens of millions, broadcasts its location to anything listening, and leaves massive coverage gaps against low-altitude threats like drones.

This architecture was built for a different era. Today's threat, swarms of cheap drones and cruise missiles flying below radar coverage, exploits every weakness of centralised, active sensing.

**What we're building**

Mentat is a passive, distributed sensing network.

* **Tracks aerial objects in 3D without emitting**: invisible to the threats it detects
* **Accurately track smaller threats**: our mesh works together to better pinpoint small targets
* **Scales via many low-cost nodes**: instead of a few high-value targets, we employ asymmetric economics where adding nodes grows linearly in cost but tracking accuracy increases exponentially

We're the sensing layer, the force multiplier for every interceptor and C-UAS system in the market.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101954&key=user_uploads/836806/ddbe92c9-897d-4e52-90ab-c8574ed7335c)

**What we're really building**

Drone detection is our wedge, not our ceiling. The real innovation isn't in any single sensor, it's in the network that ties it all together. We're building the foundational sensing and communications infrastructure layer for frontline defence. A distributed, resilient network that future defence technologies will plug into. Like the **Starlink before the Starship.**

**Why now**

Low-altitude airspace is increasingly contested. Ukraine, Nordics, Eastern Europe, & Middle East, operators everywhere are discovering that the cost curve of traditional radar doesn't scale against distributed drone threats. At the same time, edge compute, distributed systems, and passive optical sensing have reached the point where a fundamentally different architecture is viable.

**Backstory**

I spent 6+ years in Israel, living through multiple conflicts and seeing systems like Iron Dome operate against ballistic missiles and drones firsthand. When a Shahed drone exploded near my apartment, the gap between what exists and what's needed became personal. Since then, I've been in Ukraine and across Eastern Europe, working directly with military operators and validating in real conflict environments.

📍Field Test - Ukraine

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101954&key=user_uploads/836806/b380d961-dde4-4e50-b6eb-1cbf708e6d3c)

**Traction**

* Active technology demonstrations with Ukrainian military on the frontlines
* Partnerships and military relationships across USA, Ukraine, Finland, and Estonia.
* Team includes a PhD in drones/autonomy and military domain experts

name: Klaimee
long_description:
Klaimee is the first insurance for your AI agents. It covers what traditional E&O and cyber explicitly carve out, so you can deploy agentic AI at scale with real peace of mind.
Built for companies deploying agentic AI, self-serve from day one.

The problem: AI agents are taking actions autonomously buying, emailing, modifying sensitive data. AB 316 already holds deployers liable. EU AI Act enforces in August. Cyber and E&O insurance are excluding AI claims. Companies shipping agents have zero coverage and no third-party proof their agent is safe. Enterprise legal asks "who pays if your agent breaks something?" and there's no good answer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
We built the answer. Critical-category risk evaluation, certification, financial guarantee, liability insurance and the documentation enterprise procurement needs to sign off.

Team: Ines (ex-General Manager at SafetyWing, grew insurance product from $5M to $60M revenue, 5 years launching insurance products from scratch and structuring a TokioMarine MGA into its own carrier) + Julien (AI software engineer + corporate strategy, enterprise compliance).

We understand how insurance works, what enterprises require, and why startups can't wait 6 months for either.
one_liner: Liability insurance for AI Agents. You deploy agents, we cover you.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
AI agents can now execute financial transactions, access sensitive data, and take real-world actions, but there is no insurance, no certification, and no clear liability framework for when they fail.

This is the same gap that existed with cyber risk in the early 2000s, before a $15B+ insurance market emerged. We’re at that same inflection point with AI.

The signals are already there: AI-related incidents are being carved out of traditional liability coverage, lawsuits are growing rapidly, and enterprises are still under pressure to deploy AI. The result is a fast-growing, unaddressed risk layer.

We saw this firsthand. We were building AI agents for claims processing: handling payments and decisions inside regulated environments. Every customer asked the same question: who is liable when the agent gets it wrong? There was no answer.

That’s when it became clear: this infrastructure has to exist before enterprise AI can scale.

Ines had already built insurance products from zero at SafetyWing, including carrier relationships and underwriting frameworks. We realized we were uniquely positioned to build the certification and insurance layer for AI agents - so we did.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Every transformative technology needs a trust layer before it can scale.\
The internet needed cybersecurity. Cloud computing needed compliance and audit standards.

AI is next.

Today, AI agents can act but they can’t be trusted at scale. There is no standard for how they’re evaluated, no clear liability when they fail, and no infrastructure to make them safe to deploy in critical environments.

If we succeed, the liability and certification framework we build won't just protect enterprises, it will make AI itself safer, more accountable, and more auditable at a global scale. We are not just selling insurance. We are building the infrastructure that allows the agentic world to exist.

launches.body:
**TL;DR: [Klaimee](https://klaimee.ai) is the first insurance for your AI agents. It covers what traditional E&O and cyber explicitly carve out, so you can deploy agentic AI at scale with real peace of mind.**

80% of Fortune 500 companies are already using AI agents. That’s creating a new kind of liability risk no one is really covering yet.\
Enterprises want AI. But they want to know “who pays if something goes wrong”? There’s no clear answer today.\
Meanwhile, AI-related lawsuits are up 137% between 2024 and 2025.

> 👋 Hi, we are Ines and Julien.\
> [Ines](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ines-boutemadja/) was General Manager at SafetyWing (W18), she spent the last 5 years building insurance products from scratch, structured a Tokio Marine MGA, and got the Puerto Rico carrier license, scaling an insurance startup from $5M to $60M. She ran this playbook before, doing it again, AI-native this time.\
> [Julien](https://www.linkedin.com/in/julien-catonnet/) handles the engineering and enterprise compliance side. He has a strategy consulting background, working with corporates and insurance, coupled with a deep software engineering and AI expertise.\
> 🔥 Our team brings the best of both worlds to underwrite the new emerging AI risk.

### **💡 The opportunity:**

Traditional insurance was built for deterministic software; it either works or throws an explicit error. AI agents fail silently and not uniformly. So cyber won't cover it. E&O won't cover it either.

The existing insurance industry lacks the velocity and deep AI knowledge to fill this gap.

We built [Klaimee](https://klaimee.ai) to do exactly that: we provide liability insurance, financial guarantee, critical risk evaluation, certification, and procurement documentation enterprises require, all in under 24 hours.

Watch our launch video below <https://youtu.be/Y7VBNr81b5Y>

### **⚙️ How we do it:**

To insure AI agents, we had to reinvent how traditional underwriting works. Our proprietary, three-block system determines an agent’s risk score and insurance price:

1. **Public Data Scan:** We scan publicly available data related to the agent.
2. **Governance Assessment:** We ask 30 questions concerning the agent’s governance.
3. **Behavioral Testing:** We actually test your agent’s behavior, firing more than 100 probes (prompt injection, jailbreak, decision drift, data leakage, biased outputs) to understand _when_ and _how_ it fails.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100700&key=user_uploads/2955371/49d6f4de-8787-48c4-a6b2-728323148e81)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=100700&key=user_uploads/2955371/9ebe5a9c-7ce0-4d29-b3f5-c7017ca8d0d7)

**Score it. Certify it. Underwrite it. Insure it ▷ with a 24h turnaround.**

We bring the trust layers so startups and enterprises can deploy agentic AI with peace of mind.

### **🛡️ What we cover: AI agents in healthcare and biotech, finance & accounting, IT & software development, law & legal tech, customers support and sales agents.**

AI Agents act like humans: they take actions, make decisions, and have a real impact that can cause damages. At[ Klaimee](https://klaimee.ai), we cover the actual behavior of the AI agents. Real failure modes happening in production right now:

* An agent hallucinated a contract clause your customer relied on.
* An agent leaked one patient’'s data to another.
* An agent made a biased call in lending, hiring, or pricing.
* An agent took an unauthorized action with financial damage downstream.

### **⌛️ Why now:**

Major insurers like Berkshire, Chubb, and Travelers are winning state approval to exclude AI liability from standard commercial policies, leaving every agent-deploying company exposed. And it is leaving every agent-deploying company exposed.

The ISO, which sets standards for 70% of the U.S. market, is making AI exclusions the default for Commercial General Liability policies (ISO CG 40 47 / CG 40 48 endorsements). The EU AI Act enforces in August 2026.

Every Fortune 500 procurement team is now asking the AI insurance question, and the answer from incumbents is "we exclude that."

The same thing happened with cyber 20 years ago. It got carved out of existing policies. A whole new line of insurance was created. The same shift is happening with AI right now. And nobody has built the product for it yet.

Ines has done this in insurance before. Julien goes deep on the AI side. Together we know how to actually price the risk.

We understand what enterprise buyers need to see, and why a startup can’t sit around for 6 months waiting on a traditional carrier.

If you’re shipping AI agents into enterprise, you should already be thinking about coverage.

### We’re underwriting our first cohort now → [**klaimee.ai**](http://klaimee.ai)

launches.body:
# 

---

Hey everyone 👋

We’re Kyle and Kevin; co-founders of CentralComs. We’re children of landlords and are building a solution to a problem we saw all throughout our childhoods.

**TL;DR**

We run property management workflows such as **leasing, back office, and maintenance coordination workflows from start to finish,** so PM teams run smoother and earn more with the same team size.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A3NjiCcbBNY>

### **The Problem**

Property management operations are relentless, high-stakes, hands-on work built on relationships with owners, tenants, and vendors that take years to earn and seconds to lose.

It's overwhelmingly manual: **roughly 90% of the work is still manual** and extremely labor-intensive with **89% of property management companies outsourcing work** to teams overseas.

About half of leasing inquiries come in at night and on weekends, when no one's answering. **Conversion drops 7x after the first hour**.

Unresolved work orders are a top reason tenants don't renew, and **every lost renewal costs thousands** once you count turn and vacancy.

The work is rules-based and repetitive, but it demands constant attention, and missing any single step breaks the chain. That's why these roles scale so badly with headcount— you're paying for someone to be awake at the right moment to do menial tasks.

---

## **Our Solution**

**Maintenance Coordination Agent** Takes a maintenance request from submission to resolution:

* **Intake across any channel** — captures requests from email, SMS, and tenant portals, normalizing them into a single queue
* **Intelligent triage** — applies a proprietary relative and objective scoring algorithm to prioritize and triage issues in real time as conditions change
* **Smart dispatch** — routes to the right vendor based on trade, availability, and cost, sends the dispatch, and tracks confirmation
* **Persistent follow-up** — chases vendors, tenants, and owners intelligently until the job is on track and on schedule
* **Repair verification** — confirms work was actually completed via tenant sign-off, photo evidence, and vendor confirmation before closing the loop
* **Invoice processing** — validates invoices against the scope of work and approved estimates, flags discrepancies, and routes for payment approval
* **Owner & tenant updates** — keeps all parties informed at each milestone without manual outreach

**Leasing Agent** Takes a prospect from first inquiry to complete application:

* **Cross channel intake** — captures leads from listing syndication, email, SMS, web forms, and phone, normalizing them into a single queue
* **Intelligent qualification** — applies a proprietary relative and objective scoring algorithm to qualify and prioritize prospects in real time as new information comes in
* **Smart routing** — matches each lead to the right unit, schedules the tour, sends the application, and tracks completion
* **Document analysis** — reviews submitted IDs, pay stubs, and bank statements, flagging income, completeness, and inconsistencies against your criteria
* **Verification & screening** — runs identity verification and background/credit screening, then compiles a clean, decision-ready file
* **Persistent follow-up** — chases prospects intelligently until they're marked qualified

**What makes us different than traditional PMS systems?**

* We handle can handle edge cases proactively, asking for more information, reading documents, and determining the best course of action
* We don’t automate reply drafts, we send out messages, dispatch calls, retrieve missing information, and push stalled work-orders or application processes to completion.

---

## **Our Ask**

**If you answer "yes" to any of these, we'd love your help:**

* Do you know any residential property management operators whose teams are stretched thin, managing multiple systems just to keep up with maintenance and leasing?
* Do you know any property management companies looking to scale operations without increased labor cost?

**Contact**

Reach us at [**founders@centralcoms.com**](mailto:founders@centralcoms.com) or schedule a demo today at[ ](http://atlance.live/)[**centralcoms.com**](http://centralcoms.com)

launches.body:
**TLDR**: Panacea hires elite FDA regulatory consultants, and pairs them with our AI platform, to deliver **the fastest and lowest-cost pathway to FDA approval** for Biotechs and MedTechs.

<https://youtu.be/w1rudmd3cio?si=ft-e2f7QL_dBPxyj>

### **About us**

We’re Haris and Yaman. We have deep experience within enterprise AI for healthcare.

Previously, we both worked at Anterior (backed by Sequoia, NEA, Microsoft AI’s CEO) — where we built, sold and deployed our clinical AI platform to US health plans to remove major operational bottlenecks.

[Haris](https://www.linkedin.com/in/haris-javed-akhtar/) (CEO) is an MD and led partnerships on Anterior’s GTM team (2nd GTM hire), selling to the biggest healthcare enterprises in the US and landed Anterior’s first health plan and partnership customers.

[Yaman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yaman-ziadeh/) (CTO) has an MS in AI was an AI Platform Engineer, building and deploying Anterior’s clinical AI platform.

Now we’re doing the same for Life Sciences. Only this time, we’re not selling the AI tools. We’re **owning the whole stack** and selling the outcome. Faster, better and at lower cost.

### **Problem**

Developing drugs and medical devices is complex and expensive (for drugs: 10-15 years, $1-2B).

The cost of drug development is growing exponentially (doubling every 9 years). This is known as Eroom’s Law (inverse Moore’s Law).

**The most critical** process in development is getting regulatory alignment, and ultimately, approval from the FDA.

Biotechs and medtechs outsource this work to regulatory consultants.

This work is highly manual: searching through legacy FDA databases, researching and reading hundreds of publications, reading FDA guidance documents, data analysis, authoring thousands of pages per filing, etc.

Consultants take months to years, and charge 6–7 figures per engagement, to deliver FDA regulatory strategy, authoring and submission services.

These consultants also price hourly. Therefore, using AI to go faster would cannibalize their revenue. So they have no incentive to deliver work faster.

### **What changed**

**AI can automate 90% of this work**. Consultants can now focus on the 10% where their expertise and judgement is actually needed.

launches.title: ReasonBlocks - Stop your AI agents from burning money re-learning what they already know.
launches.tagline: Infra layer for smarter and cheaper AI agents
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Most production agent failures are repeats: same loops, same dead ends, same wasted tokens. Your agent doesn't learn from any of them. ReasonBlocks is a new runtime that catches failures mid-run, compresses what doesn't matter, and builds a private reasoning library that grows with every run. Result: agents that get cheaper and more reliable the more they run.

👋 We're [@Sajeev Magesh](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2796290) (ex. Stanford) and [@Rohan Vij](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3490183) (ex. CMU). We've been building together for 11 years (since 2nd grade!).

**The Problem**

Production AI agents fail in patterns. The same loops, the same redundant tool calls, the same second-guessing, happening across every customer's deployment, every day. Your agent's traces have all the information needed to prevent recurrence. Almost no system captures it.

This means:

* You're paying for the same failures repeatedly. Token bills grow without agents getting better.
* Trajectories are inconsistent, your agent re-solves the same kind of task differently each time.
* No compounding improvement: your 10,000th run is no smarter than your 1st.

**What We Built**

ReasonBlocks sits in your agent runtime and does three things:

1. **Catches failures mid-run.** Six monitors watch every agent call for loops, redundant work, and second-guessing. When one fires, a correction gets injected before tokens are wasted.
2. **Compresses what doesn't matter.** Stale tool outputs and redundant context get cut from the message history automatically. Your context stays focused, your bill stays small.
3. **Captures every lesson into a private reasoning library.** After each run, the system extracts what worked and adds it to your library. Patterns get matched and injected into future runs automatically. Your library is yours, built from your production data, growing every day.

This isn't just per-task memory. It's a runtime that turns every agent run into something the next run can use.

Integrate with one command. Works with any model, any framework.

**Results**

On SWE-bench Pro (75 problems, Sonnet 4.6):

* 42% accuracy gain
* 52% token reduction with combined monitor + compression stack
* 70% fewer budget cap-hits

**Our Asks**

1. **Try it out** — our platform and SDK are live at [reasonblocks.com](http://reasonblocks.com).
2. **Intros welcome** — if you or anyone you know is building vertical AI agents (legal, finance, healthcare, security, research) running at scale, we'd love to chat.
3. **Feedback** — we're early and learning fast. Tell us what's broken, what's missing, what you'd need to deploy this in production.

DM either of us anytime!

Hey YC! We’re [Hang Huang](https://linkedin.com/in/hang-huang-oliver) and [Tony Chang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tony-chang-0430/) from [InsForge](https://insforge.dev/).

**TL;DR:** InsForge lets your AI coding agent deploy and operate the full backend (servers, database, auth, storage, and more) from one consistent CLI. Instead of stitching together separate tools and dashboards, your agent manage entire backend infrastructure end-to-end.

<https://youtu.be/7Bax5qz0IfM>

**The Problem**

The way software gets built is changing fast. Coding agents are now the primary builders, but every backend platform today was designed for human developers, with dashboards, manual configs, and workflows that require a person at every step.

We tried MCP servers like Supabase, Vercel, GitHub, and Context7, but kept running into the same problems: tools bloated the context window, payloads came back at 10K+ tokens, and core backend state like telemetry, configs, logs, and runtime behavior still wasn’t accessible in a way agents could reliably use.

**Our Solution**

So we built InsForge as one backend platform your coding agent can actually operate. Install our CLI and Skills with one command, and your coding agent can build, run, debug, and scale full-stack apps end to end on InsForge.

Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors the agent can act on. And because agents make mistakes, branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes let you review or discard changes safely.

**Where We're Going**

We believe that coding agents won’t stop at writing code. They’ll run your entire application and infrastructure autonomously as well. For that to work, backend infrastructure needs to become agent-native: CLI-first, observable, permissioned, reversible, and designed around agents as operators.

\
Launch video: <https://youtube.com/shorts/6XySjjG9KNA?si=zb2bP4_0sqMfYz62>

# Your AI doesn’t even know

You’re automating the boring work with agents so you can build more, faster. BUT:

* Agents forget your customers + your relationships
* Agents ignore know your taste, and code smelly, ugly features
* Agents can’t remember your pivots, and act on stale data
* Agents keep making the same mistakes over and over, no matter how many times you yell at them.

So you’ve tried some insane manual hacks:

* You paste dumps of the same context into every new chat.
* You write obvious skills for something that it should just "know".
* You commit markdown files in your codebase so everyone's AI is on the same page.
* You hack an off-the-shelf memory libraries to fit your unique story

…before you know it, you have a huge mess of broken agents, and no amount of pasting, screenshotting, or committing gives your AI the complete, living picture of your company.

# ENTER: HYPER

**Hyper fixes all of this without you having to do anything.**

1. Hyper quietly pulls out important info from every document, calendar invite, email, Slack, GitHub pull request, conversation, and more.

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/2474cd22-beeb-4525-bc19-bd546bd3a91e)

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/d727c84a-929b-44a9-b1de-283717b3f134)

   ![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101226&key=user_uploads/2784940/e019494b-f3a9-4d81-8ff9-14b16168aa63)


Now your AI knows: _Who did we talk to last week? What customer is facing this bug? How much revenue do we need before next week’s meeting?_

But it also knows: _What’s our design philosophy? What sales strategy seems to work best with mid-level execs? What feedback isn’t worth paying attention to right now?_

Hyper builds this brain across your whole company — so the next time your agents get to work, they _just know_. And the next time your teammates sit down to work, _they just know too._

**Kanyes** helped secure multi-million dollar deals at Snorkel AI and wrote motion algorithms at Matic Robots. Hey YC 👋\
\
We’re Rayan and Maadhav, and today we’re excited to launch [Enjamb Labs](https://www.enjamb.ai/).

<https://youtu.be/5DwdtiLvViM>\
\
**TL;DR**

Enjamb runs the entire drug program for biopharma teams, from discovery to FDA approval. \
\
Pharma runs on decades of closed legacy systems like Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, and SAS, with no AI layer and no MCP to connect agents to them. So we built that connection layer. \
\
Our agents run on top of their existing systems and data, with no migration, and do the work across the whole program: clinical evidence, trial design, statistical programming, and regulatory submissions.\
\
In just 3 weeks since launch, we're already being used by 500+ employees at top pharma companies, including Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Merck & Sanofi.

**The Problem: Pharma’s systems have no AI layer**

It costs $2.6 billion and 10+ years to ship a single drug, and most of that isn't the science. It's the work around it, spread across decades of closed legacy systems that don't talk to each other:

* Benchling stores the data
* Veeva holds the documents
* Medidata runs the trials
* SAS does the stats

Agents are **_finally_**  good enough to do real scientific work. But there's no AI layer on these systems, and no MCP to plug an agent into where pharma's data and work actually live.

**So, we built that connection layer we wished existed.**\
\
**What We Offer: Agents that run on top of pharma’s existing systems**

Enjamb invented the fastest way to run a drug program: a single agentic workspace that unifies the evidence, analysis, and regulatory work.

Our agents:

* Synthesize up-to-date clinical evidence from the literature and real-world data to pinpoint the right endpoints and patient populations
* Design trials and run the statistical programming behind them, including SDTM, ADaM, TFLs, and QC
* Draft and audit regulatory documents like INDs, protocols, SAPs, and NDAs

— all in one auditable workspace, with the context carried end to end.\

**And it all runs in the browser**: full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint editors, a Python and R compute environment, 100+ scientific integrations, and 50+ fine-tuned models for in-silico validation. No setup.

**Our Story: Two Researchers Who Lived the Problem**

We kept hitting the same wall in research: the science was the easy part. Everything around it, the evidence, the analysis, the documents, was fragmented, manual, and disconnected, and the context died at every handoff.\
\
So we built what we always wanted: one workspace where agents carry the context across the entire drug program.

**If no one's going to build it right, we will.**\
\

launches.body:
**The Problem**

Credentialing and contracting determine which clinicians can bill insurance, and at what rate. Today, both are broken processes: slow, fragmented, and almost entirely manual. Healthcare organizations are forced to juggle dozens of documents, third-party verifications, and follow-ups across hundreds of payer portals with unique requirements and timelines.

The result: revenue is delayed, contract terms go unnegotiated, payers deny clinicians, and patient access is restricted. 

**Our Solution**

Arctic Health hires best-in-class credentialing experts and pairs them with our AI platform to deliver the fastest and lowest-cost path to contracting and payer enrollment for healthcare organizations of any size.

We handle the end-to-end workflow, from establishing payer contracts to enrolling each provider. We collect and validate organization and provider data according to each state and payer’s requirements, and submit on the organization's behalf. We then monitor status and compliance on an ongoing basis.

The platform gets smarter with every submission, contract, and claim. Our browser agents learn to navigate payer portals more effectively. Our communications data shows us who to reach at each payer and when. Enrollment outcomes reveal which networks are actually open. And as we handle negotiations across payers and networks, we build a clearer picture of how contracts get done and how rates vary by specialty and region.

**Our Backstory**

At our previous companies (Scale AI, Instabase, and Airbnb) we kept running into the same gap: powerful AI tools fell short in workflows with specific rules, data types, and consequences. Nowhere was that gap more visible than in US healthcare, where administrative spend exceeds $1T annually. We decided it was time to close the gap. We started with credentialing and contracting, workflows that cost billions each year and were in desperate need of the solution we envisioned: AI that understands documents and executes guidelines precisely, eliminating overhead. 

**The Team**

Before that, he developed the payroll platform and mobile app at Zenefits. Most recently, he co-founded and scaled Handstamp, an event ticketing platform, to several million in GMV and hundreds of thousands of users.

Hello! We’re [Tane](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tanekim/) and [David](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-cui-589a20228/), co-founders of [Framewise Health](https://framewisehealth.com).

# **TL;DR**

**Framewise Health turns medical records into personalized videos that walk patients through onboarding, adherence, and recovery.** The data we collect lets hospitals and clinics spend less time chasing patients and more time caring for them.

**_Ask_:** Can you introduce us to specialty clinic owners, hospital service-line chiefs, patient experience VPs, or pharma medical affairs leads? Contact us at [tane@framewisehealth.com](mailto:tane@framewisehealth.com)

Launch video: <https://youtu.be/ri6U0W8frFU>

# **The Problem**

Nearly 9 out of 10 people in the U.S. lack proficient health literacy.

Yet, our healthcare system has relied on educating patients using complex paper packets for decades, leaving us with static, generic solutions that cause three problems:

* Ineffective learning
* Low medical adherence
* Poor patient outcomes

Preventable medication-related harm costs the U.S. over $500 billion every year.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101156&key=user_uploads/3115980/d644d1d2-1da6-4aec-8a1e-13dae6d1a309)

Until now, there was no cost-effective way to create personalized education material for patients. But with the latest video generation models, this no longer has to be the case.

# **Our Solution**

Every video is generated from the patient's medical records, institutional protocols, and national drug data. Every patient interaction tells you what they understood, per patient, per topic, in real time. 

That comprehension data feeds back to the care team, so they know which patients are on track and which need a callback.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101156&key=user_uploads/3115980/06903869-3f1e-4802-b6de-f36937a2b3b4)

# **How can you help?**

If you can introduce us to any of the following, we’d be grateful.

* Hospitals (service-line chiefs, CMIOs, virtual health program leads, VPs of patient experience)
* Pharma (medical affairs leads on adherence, patient services VPs, clinical education directors)
* Private clinics (practice owners in procedure-heavy specialties)

Please contact us at [tane@framewisehealth.com](mailto:tane@framewisehealth.com)

# **Who we are**

Tane and David met during Brown University’s freshman orientation.

Tane (CEO) dropped out of Brown’s BS/MD program and saw 500+ patient interactions at over a dozen institutions. 

David (CTO) researched computer vision at Brown and was an engineering intern at a YC voice AI company (Freya S25).
